en.regest: Konrad am Wasen, who was punished with banishment from the city, asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for safe conduct so that he may still settle his affairs in the city.

Rudolf Wingarter von Lichtensteig, Amtmann of Count Friedrich von Toggenburg, asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to help Anna Etterlin in an inheritance matter. She will give more information about this orally.
Johannes Thiliger asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to have a reply to his application as schoolmaster in St. Gallen sent to him by the messenger.

Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to deliberate on how to proceed with the collection of the annual interest outstanding from Counts Rudolf and Wilhelm von Montfort of Tettnang. St. Gallen is to send an authorized Council delegation to Konstanz on the evening of 30 November to deliberate on this matter.

Burgomaster and Council of Schaffhausen address Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen with the request to ensure with the Abbot of the Benedictine monastery that a scribe, who has taken a book written for the parish church of Schaffhausen with him to St. Gallen, in order perhaps to show it to the Abbot of the Benedictine monastery of St. Gallen and to receive a commission, hands the book over to the messenger, since the parish church can no longer do without the book.

Brother Ulrich Zeph von Rüti asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to ensure that Friedrich Stüdeli settles his debts with him (Ulrich Zeph); Stüdeli had received money from Heinrich Zeph on account of the already deceased Hans Zeph. He hopes for an out-of-court settlement, does not shy away from a court hearing if it should prove necessary, and asks for a written reply.

Rudolf, Heinrich, Hans, Friedrich von Tettikofen and Konrad in der Bünt, called Rüll of Konstanz, ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen not to punish Georg Wildrich, who was taken prisoner for an offense, harshly, but to release him against the provision of a modest surety. They ask for a written answer.

Burgomaster and Council of Markdorf request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to urge the siblings of Anna Garnleder, whom their citizen Peter Küng has married, the daughter of the deceased citizen of St. Gallen Heinrich Garnleder, to pay him the portion of the paternal inheritance that is due to her. In the event of a lawsuit, they request the support of St. Gallen.

Ulrich Gnäpser, citizen of St. Gallen, asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to speak with Georg Wildrich, who has brought a charge against him and Wetzel Völi for the murder of Wildrich's brother. Gnäpser shows himself ready to answer for himself before the court and to accept a judgment, but asks for safe conduct. In addition, he asks for a written answer with the same messenger.

Ursula von Roggwil, citizen of Konstanz, urges Ulrich Gössler, citizen of St. Gallen, to pay her annuity, which is due to her from the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen and for which Gössler is surety.

Johannes Thiliger, schoolmaster in Kempten, asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for help in collecting school fees that several citizens of St. Gallen, whose children he had been teaching, still owed him.

The physician Dietrich Walke asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to ensure that the outstanding treatment costs for several citizens of St. Gallen and in particular for the widow of a Spiser are paid. Should the payments not be made, he will proceed legally against the debtors.

King Sigismund writes to the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen, that they should give credence to the statements of his councillors Brunoro della Scala, Vikar in Verona and Vicenza, Wilhelm, Count of Prata, and Johannes, called Melonensibus, of Prata, teacher of ecclesiastical law, in the matter concerning Kaspar Torner, as if he were instructing them himself.

Ammann and countrymen of Glarus ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for the protection of the priest Hans Kessler from a Herr von Ramschwag, their citizen, and his (St. Gallen) helpers. They ask for a written answer with the same messenger.

Burgomaster and Council of Zürich inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that they will decide at the negotiation in Winterthur on 23. January to strike a new coin. They ask the St. Gallen to send their envoys and to decide whether the St. Gallen will participate in this coin renewal. Zürich wants to issue the new coins on 5. March and the contract is to be valid for five years.

Burgomaster and Council of Zürich report to Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen, in response to their written inquiry, how Zürich intends to proceed after the negotiations on the subject of new coinage. Zürich invites St. Gallen to further negotiations in Winterthur on 11 January, to which they are to send envoys. At the same time, they wish to receive a written statement of intent in advance.

Burgomaster and Council of Zürich, who wish to consult together with the Confederates of Bern, Solothurn and Luzern on a new coinage, invite Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to participate in a negotiation in Aarau on 25 November. A similar invitation has been sent to Schaffhausen, with the request that the envoys of St. Gallen and Schaffhausen consult with them, the Zürchers, before the negotiation.

Werner Ehinger, citizen of Konstanz, asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to readmit his female relative, sister Ursula Schlichting, to the Klause in St. Gallen, especially since the Klause has been rebuilt after the fire with the help of him and other of her friends. He asks for a written answer.

Polikarpus, parish priest at Marbach, defends himself against the complaint brought before the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen by Anna Steingachter, who alleges that she is pregnant by him. He says that he will not defend himself before the court, as accusations previously raised by this woman against him turned out to be slander.

Konrad Utz von St. Gallen asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to inform him in writing how he is to conduct himself in the face of the accusations of the Appenzellers. They had taken him prisoner despite a letter of safe conduct and forced him to make sworn statements, as they would otherwise drown him. The Bishop of Konstanz had already released him from the oath towards the Appenzellers.

Burgomaster and Council of Zürich inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that they had also concluded a truce until 11 November, in the name of St. Gallen as well, with Duke Reinold von Urslingen and Count Eitel Fritz von Hohenzollern, with whom they and the Confederates allied with them are at war on account of Hans Gruber, and also on account of Konrad, Rudolf and Ulrich Brotbeck, brothers from Niederneunforn, as well as on account of Kaspar Meyer von Baden.

Ulrich Zeph, priest at Arbon, asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to support his brother Heinrich, who had taken in their father. Ulrich Zeph renounces the paternal inheritance in favor of his brother Heinrich; excluded from this is a debt of his father to him, Ulrich, of 30 pounds.

Ulrich Gnäpser, who has killed Hans Wildrich, asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for support in court against Georg Wildrich and others. The latter (Georg Wildrich) had let the ban be pronounced against him. Ulrich Gnäpser complains that Georg Wildrich was allowed to appear before a foreign court; he asks for a written answer.
Hans Zeph asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to assist his brother Heinrich regarding their mentally confused father.

Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to assist the messenger of the Jewess Jenkle in the collection of debts that several citizens of St. Gallen would have with her.

Heinrich von Mansdorf, Abbot of the Benedictine monastery of St. Gallen, asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to assist him in the redemption of a tenth at Höchst on behalf of Ulrich Estrich.

Heinrich von Mansdorf, Abbot of the Benedictine monastery of St. Gallen, asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to admonish their citizen Ulrich Estrich, from whom the monastery had redeemed the tithe of Höchst and had pledged it to Werner Ehinger of Konstanz. Estrich is to prevent Ehinger from being hindered in the pledge and not to cause the monastery any trouble, otherwise the Abbot must proceed against Estrich in court. He asks for a written answer with the same messenger.
Ammann and Council of Rheineck ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to grant them an extension of the deadline for the repayment of a debt until the next autumn.

Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to postpone the negotiation between Hans Weninger, citizen of St. Gallen, and Peter Ruprecht, citizen of Konstanz, because Ruprecht wishes to await a reply from Rome and the Burgomaster will also be absent on the fixed date.

Wilhelm Fisch informs the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen about rumors of arson that had been spread about him by people of St. Gallen, among others by Ulrich Hätzler, and asks for a written answer with the same messenger whether he is safe before them and their people.
Eglolf Blarer, abbot of the Benedictine monastery of St. Gallen, asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for considerate treatment of Wilhelm Fisch, who was taken prisoner by them.
Otmar Ortwin von St. Gallen complains to the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen about the seizure of the property of him and his wife. He asks for a written reply with the same messenger.

Hans Schad, called Güggel, asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to compel Sigmund, called Münzer, from whom he had borrowed a coat worth one gulden and to whom he himself had lent one worth 12 gulden, to return his coat to him or to compensate him for the difference in value.

Otmar Ortwin and Hans Mayer apologize to the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for not having kept an appointment in St. Gallen. The request for it had arrived too late and they had committed themselves to a commission of the Bishop of Basel. They ask for an extension of the deadline until they can come to St. Gallen. They ask for a written answer.

Ammann and the country people of Glarus ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen, at the request of their (Glarus) parish priest Hans Kessler, for help. It concerns the question of whether his marriage is legally valid or not; his cousin Johannes Kupferschmid has already traveled to Rome in this matter. Glarus asks for an immediate written answer.

Elisabeth Estrich von St. Gallen complains to the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that she has received no answer to a previous letter of complaint. She does not wish to accept that she is being pursued by the Burgomaster and Council for a physical assault committed against her by Hans Pfister and his daughter. She also does not wish to accept that Hans Pfister and his daughter are not to be punished by St. Gallen, because, according to the reasoning of the Burgomaster and Council, the two are not citizens of St. Gallen. She asks for a written answer with the same messenger.

Eglolf Blarer, Abbot of the Benedictine monastery of St. Gallen, asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to restrain their fellow citizen Ulrich Estrich from hindering the monastery and Werner Ehinger of Konstanz from the use of the tithe at Höchst, which had been pledged to Werner Ehinger by the predecessor abbot Heinrich von Mansdorf. Furthermore, Estrich is to restore the prevented use of the tithe of the last year. The Abbot asks for a written answer with the same messenger.

Burgomaster and Council of Buchhorn inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that, according to their Gredmeister, the widow of Heinz Fridank, a citizen of Buchhorn, is retaining the iron of the St. Gallen citizen Heinrich Zwick senior in the Grede as security for a debt of money owed by Zwick to Fridank for sea transports. Buchhorn asks St. Gallen to intervene for the settlement of the debt and requests a written answer.

Elisabeth Lind, called Estrichin, writes again to the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen, saying that she does not know what fault she has committed, and asks for an answer with the same messenger as to how she should conduct herself.

Burgomaster and Council of Schaffhausen inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that Konrad Barter, citizen of Schaffhausen, has claims to the inheritance of the deceased Bilgeri Fisch through his wife, the sister of the deceased Bilgeri Fisch. Parter asks St. Gallen to take the estate of his deceased brother-in-law Fisch into custody until he himself can come to St. Gallen.

Bartholomäus Keller, citizen of St. Gallen, asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to intervene with the Appenzellers for a peaceful settlement of the conflict he has with them over a homicide. He asks for support and a written answer to the house of the bailiff of Bürglen.
Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that Lindau, which, like St. Gallen, is in dispute with Bregenz, has also agreed to a peace until 23 April.

Ammann and Council of Appenzell request, on behalf of their countryman Walter Koppenhan senior, from Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen legal assistance in a dispute with the citizens of St. Gallen Hans Stahel, Egli Kessler and Hans am Egglin. The Appenzellers request a written reply with the same messenger.

Ammann and Council of Appenzell ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to ensure that the peace agreed upon between their countryman Egli Oswald and the citizens of St. Gallen Hans Ghüssit and Hans Schnider is observed by the latter. They ask for a reply with the same messenger.

Ammann and Council of Appenzell ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to ensure the safety and protection of their countryman Heinrich im Rain. They ask for a written reply with the same messenger.

Otto III. von Hachberg, Bishop of Konstanz, asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to allow their schoolmaster, who has committed himself to Konstanz, to take up his position in Konstanz at the next Whitsun (20. Mai).

Jakob Bart, Pfarrer und Chorherr im Chorherrenstift St. Stephan zu Konstanz, recommends a new schoolmaster to the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen. He says that the latter cannot yet present himself in person in St. Gallen, as he is still occupied in Schaffhausen. He asks for a reply.

Captain, Ammann and Council of Appenzell again request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to ensure that their (St. Gallen) citizen Hans Ghüssit keeps the agreed peace with their (Appenzell) countryman Egli Oswald. They would in turn hold Oswald to this. They request a written answer with the same messenger.

Burgomaster and Council of Überlingen ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to ensure that the statements of their master mason Niklaus, stonemason at Salem, are not taken amiss in St. Gallen. They ask for a written reply with the messenger.
Hans Frank informs Berchtold Gudler, toll collector at the Kaufhaus in Ulm, in a second letter about the conclusion of a purchase of 100 Scheiben Wachs by Peter von Watt.

Burgomaster and Council of Radolfzell ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to support their (Radolfzell) citizen Siegfried Plütsch in a private matter. Plütsch will show this letter and present his matter orally.

Burgomaster and Council of Überlingen complain to Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that their citizens Rudolf Gelter and Särri have not yet settled their debts despite a request already made. They ask that their messenger and bearer of the letter be assisted in the collection of the debt.

Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to support their (Konstanz) citizen Elisabeth Kupferschmid, whose husband Georg Kupferschmid had been murdered in the Rheintal, in the resolution of the case.

Konrad Storchenegger writes to the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen, saying that he has been informed that he is no longer safe in his life within the territory of St. Gallen, and asks that a written answer be sent to him with the same messenger.

Burgomaster and Council of Isny ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to let justice be done to their (Isny) citizen Frick Ledler the Younger in a dispute over an interest, which had been situated on the house of Frick Ledler the Elder.
Albrecht Blarer, Domherr zu Konstanz, recommends to the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen Kaspar Netzer as the new schoolmaster, after having heard that the previous schoolmaster had moved away.

Ammann and Council of Appenzell request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to release the confiscated property of their countryman Hans Maier, called Schärrer. They request a written reply with the same messenger.

Ammann and Council of Appenzell ask for the umpteenth time Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to release the confiscated property of their countryman Hans Maier, called Schärrer. He claims that he owes the city of St. Gallen money on account of a fine, but neither taxes nor Ungeld. They ask for a written answer with the same messenger.
Ammann and Council of Appenzell inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that Otmar Ortwin has accepted the Landrecht with them.

Ammann and Council of Appenzell inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that the Lords of Rorschach, citizens of St. Gallen, are threatening their fellow countryman Frick Köbili. They ask St. Gallen to protect Köbili from the Rorschachers and to send them a written reply with the same messenger.

Ammann and Council of Appenzell inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that their (St. Gallen) citizen, Koppenhan the Elder, who is in a legal dispute with Uli Schläpfer, is safe as long as he adheres to the already issued judicial decision.

Ammann and Council of Appenzell ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to settle the dispute between their (Appenzell) countrymen Junker Estrich and his wife and Otmar Ortwin before their (St. Gallen) court.

Ammann and Council of Appenzell inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen about several disputes concerning peasants of Appenzell and citizens of St. Gallen. The citizen of St. Gallen Hans Tobler is to pay taxes to the Appenzellers for his properties located there, the dispute between Herman Höger of Herisau and Peter and Heinrich Zwicker is to be settled, and Walter Koppenhan has come before the court with Kueni Schedler.

Eglolf Blarer, Abbot of the Benedictine monastery of St. Gallen, complains to the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that several citizens of St. Gallen had broken into the monastery at night and plundered his wine cellar. He asks for an investigation and the punishment of those involved.

Eglolf Blarer, Abbot of the Benedictine monastery of St. Gallen, complains to the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that Hans von Andwil has not vacated the house in the cloister belonging to the monastery, which he had previously inhabited, despite requests from the monastery. The Abbot asks for help.

Eglolf Blarer, abbot of the Benedictine monastery of St. Gallen, complains to the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that they did not appropriately support his bailiff in court in the dispute with Hans von Andwil. The abbot also asks that they ensure that Andwil ends his ill will, otherwise he would consider further steps.

Eglolf Blarer, Abbot of the Benedictine monastery of St. Gallen, complains to the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen about their (St. Gallen) manner of collecting taxes from people in Gossau, Bernhardzell and elsewhere, some of whom are citizens of St. Gallen.

Walter Koppenhan der Jüngere asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for understanding regarding the renunciation of his citizenship of St. Gallen, thanks them for the good relationship, and hopes to be able to count on their support in the future as well, if needed.

Friedrich III. von Zollern, Bishop of Konstanz, informs the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen about a Visitation in the Benedictine monastery of St. Gallen that he did not authorize and asks that the disobedient be sent to him.
Burgomaster and Council of Ulm request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to actively support one of their citizens at a court day before the abbot of the Benedictine monastery of St. Gallen.

The messengers of the Confederates from Zürich, Luzern, Uri, Schwyz, Unterwalden, Zug and Glarus ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to hand over Hans Vögeli if he should be in their territory. They ask for a written answer with the same messenger.

The weaver Johannes Brunner asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to hand over to his wife and children their property, which apparently has been confiscated on account of a Hans Wechsler from Salzburg. Should the Council not agree to this, he (Johannes Brunner) says that he will proceed against it before other courts. He asks for mediation and a written answer.

Lewo Locher complains to the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen about malicious slander against him, because his master Ulrich has debts in Holz. He swears that he knew nothing of the debts, and offers his support. He asks for a written answer.

Johannes Häch, priest in Sommeri, complains to the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that Friedrich Stüdeli and his son Matthias had repeatedly pressured him to ride with them to Konstanz to help them in a matter. In the end, father and son had refused to compensate him. Johannes Häch asks for support and threatens to bring the two before the ecclesiastical court in Konstanz. He asks for a reply with the same messenger.
Burgomaster and Council of Schaffhausen ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to allow Hans Barter, the son of the Schaffhausen citizen Konrad Barter, to move to his mother in Schaffhausen.

Burgomaster and Council of Lindau inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that Eglolf von Rorschach the Younger has complained to the Emperor that Lindau had admitted people of his (Eglolf's) as citizens. They state that they are not willing to negotiate on this matter and ask St. Gallen to act so that Eglolf von Rorschach takes no further steps, as this would be to the detriment of all cities. They ask for a written answer.

Burgomaster and Council of Rottweil ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to support their citizen Georg von Zell, the bearer of the letter, who is in a dispute with the furrier Heinz Lutzer, a citizen of St. Gallen. The St. Gallen authorities are to let justice be done to the Rottweil citizen.

Burgomaster and Council of Lindau ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to speak with Eberhard Brisig and his barber's servant, so that the latter, who has obligated himself to work for Master Martin Dorn, a member of the Council of Lindau, may finally take up his position in Lindau. They ask for a written answer.

Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to send a Council delegation to Ravensburg on the coming 10. August to consult with other Imperial cities on the coinage, meat trade, and other matters. They (Konstanz) are of the opinion that it is necessary to reach a consensus with the cities in the vicinity on this and to maintain it.

Burgomaster and Council of Lindau ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen, in their dispute with the Lords of Rorschach, to seek the opinion of the Rorschach residents regarding renewed negotiations. In addition, the Lindau residents ask for support with a St. Gallen Council delegation.

Heinrich von Sigberg and the two brothers Hans and Hans Tumb von Neuburg ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to provide them with a Council delegation, in particular Konrad Hör or, in his absence, the town Ammann, for a negotiation with the women's community in Altstätten.

Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz remind Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen of the past meeting of the Imperial Cities in Buchhorn, at which the negotiations had not reached a goal. Therefore, the Konstanzer invite the St. Galler to a next meeting in Ravensburg on 12 September, so that the negotiations could continue there.

Hans Tumb von Neuburg asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to inform Michael von Ems and Dietegen von Grünenstein that he has deposited 900 pounds of redemption money for his wife with the Council of Lindau.

Burgomaster and Council of Lindau request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to send their Council delegation to negotiate the conflict with the Lords of Rorschach regarding the admission of citizens on 12 September to Konstanz. This matter concerns the rights and freedoms of all cities.

Burgomaster and Council of Buchhorn inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that their (Buchhorn) citizen Hans Riederer had been unlawfully evicted from a farm which had been granted to him for six years by the Holy Spirit Hospital of St. Gallen. They ask for help and clarification as well as for a written or oral reply with the same messenger.

Ammann and Council of Appenzell, in the name of their countryman Heinrich Weisshaar, direct a request to Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to ensure that his property, which was seized by the former Burgomaster of St. Gallen Ulrich Särri and by Nesa Dietz, be released again. They ask for a written reply with the same messenger.
Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to send a Council delegation to a consultation at which the felling of oaks is to be discussed.

Dorothea von Altstätten informs the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that the negotiations in the dispute between those of Lustenau and Höchst had remained unsuccessful. The messenger and bearer of this letter sent to her can report on this. She asks for further support.

Burgomaster and Council of Schaffhausen repeatedly request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to ensure that the balances and interest owed by St. Gallen to Hans and Verena, the children of Konrad Barters wife, are paid. The children have moved to their mother in Schaffhausen and have accepted the citizenship there. Schaffhausen requests a written reply with the same messenger.

Statthalter and Council of Appenzell ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to help them in the investigation of the homicide of their Ammann Häch. St. Gallen is to question its runner Konrad Utz, witness to the crime, as to who had been helpers of the murderer named Himmeli.
Albrecht Tumb von Neuburg asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to support him at a court hearing in Appenzell with a delegation of St. Gallen.
Burgomaster and Council of Lindau inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that they had set the court day in the dispute between Eberhard von Ramschwag and Hans von Ems for 8 July.
Burgomaster and Council of Lindau inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that the previously set court day in the dispute between Eberhard von Ramschwag and Hans von Ems has been postponed.

Burgomaster and Council of Lindau answer Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen on the St. Gallen request to let the court day in the dispute between Eberhard von Ramschwag and Hans von Ems remain on the agreed day, and agree to it.

Burgomaster and Council of Lindau complain to Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that their grain merchants do not adhere to the agreements and secretly buy their grain in unlicensed border places. Lindau asks St. Gallen to reprimand their grain buyers. If the grain market were moved to the villages, this would harm the towns and the countryside.

Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz write to Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen, that they would ensure a settlement of the dispute of the quarrelsome lantern-maker of Konstanz with the citizen of St. Gallen Konrad Kurlimann.

Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for help in a dispute between Ulrich Streif and Heinrich von Miltenberg over bad copper. St. Gallen is to question their citizen Ulrich Schnabelburg, to whom Miltenberg had sold the same goods two years ago. They ask for a written reply with the same messenger.

Burgomaster and Council of Überlingen ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for a proposal on how the complaints of the butchers of Überlingen and St. Gallen regarding their treatment in Konstanz vis-à-vis the citizens of Konstanz are to be submitted jointly. They ask for a written reply with the same messenger.
Burgomaster and Council of Lindau inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that the Emperor has died. Burgomaster and Council of Ulm had reported this to them.

Captain, Ammann and Council of Appenzell inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that one of their countrymen, Ulrich Himmeli, was found in the house of the young Koppenhan in Überlingen. The Appenzell people ask the St. Gallen people to arrest the old Koppenhan, since he knows that Himmeli is their common enemy.

Marquard der Jüngere von Schellenberg asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to help him in the collection of a debt from the citizen of St. Gallen Eberhard von Ramschwag, the son-in-law and heir of Ulrichs von Ems, the original debtor. He asks for the appointment of a day of negotiation and for a written answer with the messenger.

Marquard der Jüngere von Schellenberg answers the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that he will not waive his claim against their citizen Eberhard von Ramschwag and will therefore attend the day of negotiation appointed by them.

Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that the term set for 23 April in Buchhorn cannot be kept. The Ravensburgers had already, before this invitation, invited them to Ravensburg and ask the St. Gallen to send their Council delegation there as well. Furthermore, they add that the Ravensburgers had written to them that the meat purchase must absolutely be discussed on this occasion.
Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that they have already sent them a response the day before concerning the citizen of St. Gallen Hans Mötteli.

Marquard von Schellenberg asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to intervene on his behalf with their citizen Eberhard von Ramschag, so that the latter issues to him the promised debt instrument guaranteed by Hug von Watt. He asks for a written reply with the messenger.

Burgomaster and Council of Lindau ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen, on behalf of their citizen Martin Ruf, to press their citizen Heinrich Benst von Lustenau to pay the interest that he has owed to Martin Ruf's stepchildren for six years, or else Benst should accept the sale of the properties from which the interest is to be paid. They ask for a written answer with the messenger.

Burgomaster and Council of Lindau write in a matter between the St. Gallen citizen Friedrich von Gossolt and the Ravensburg citizen Mosheim. Since Gossolt does not wish to appear in Lindau for a day of negotiation, St. Gallen should ensure that Gebhard von Schellenberg in Bregenz, Rheineck or Arbon holds a day of negotiation. Ravensburg will also ask Schellenberg to do so.

Ulrich von Eisenhofen, bailiff of Feldkirch, asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to inform him how their citizen Rudolf von Rorschach, who raises monetary claims against their lord, the Duke of Österreich, stands with regard to the legal offers made so far. Should he not wish to accept any of them, the Feldkirch side proposes a day of negotiation before the Imperial bailiff, at which it is to be clarified whether Feldkirch may be sued by him for the debts that the Duke of Österreich owes the St. Gallen citizen Rudolf von Rorschach. They ask for a written answer with the messenger.

Burgomaster and Council of Lindau inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that the citizen of Lindau Martin Ruf will come to St. Gallen on 1 September on the day of negotiation set by St. Gallen, in the dispute with Heinrich Benst concerning interest which the latter owes to the stepchildren of Ruf, to represent himself and the children.

Burgomaster and Council of Lindau inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that they would issue the letter, requested by St. Gallen, addressed to Friedrich von Brandenburg and his Landrichter at Nürnberg, Wilhelm von Hohenrechberg, in favor of the citizen of St. Gallen, Hans Mötteli, who had been summoned before the Landgericht Nürnberg by Hans Arnold. If the messenger passed through Lindau, the letter would be ready and could be taken by him.

Burgomaster and Council of Lindau ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to compel their citizen Wilhelm Blarer zu Wartensee to return the property of the Lindau citizen Johann Tudeller, which Blarer has seized. If Blarer has legitimate claims against Tudeller, he is to make them before the Lindau court. The Lindau authorities ask for a written reply with the messenger.

Ulrich von Eisenhofen, bailiff of Feldkirch, who on behalf of his lordship of Österreich has seized wine from the abbot of the Benedictine monastery of St. Gallen and brought it to the court of Rheineck, asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to send a council delegation to the negotiation of 17 November. The Burgomaster of St. Gallen has already been informed of this by Othmar Litscher, Amtmann in the County of Feldkirch.

Burgomaster and Council of Lindau ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to persuade the citizen of St. Gallen Wilhelm von Steinach to hand over the paternal inheritance to the wife of Johann Seckler. Should Steinach not be willing to do so, he should at least agree to a negotiation in Lindau. The Lindauers ask for a written answer with the messenger.

Wolfhart der Ältere von Brandis asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to restrain their citizen named Bingesser from his ill deeds and slander against him and his heirs, and to substantiate the claims that this man and his brother Stüdlin were making before a court with witnesses. Brandis asks for a written answer with the messenger.

Dorothea von Altstätten informs the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that her Ammann of Lustenau will come to them in a matter that concerns her and the Ammann. The Ammann will lay out the matter, and she asks the St. Gallen for support.
Wolfhart von Brandis asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to send their Burgomaster Gelter to Bludenz on the evening of 22 February for a negotiation.

Friedrich III. von Habsburg-Österreich asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to restrain their citizen Eberhard von Ramschwag from changing anything in the legal status of a farm, as this is an imperial fief. The Duke asks the St. Gallen authorities for a written answer.

Burgomaster and Council of Lindau request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to send a Council delegation to Buchhorn, where the dispute between the citizens of Lindau and Count Wilhelm von Montfort, Lord of Tettnang, is to be further negotiated on 20 April. In particular, the town clerk is also to be present.

Johann, Count zu Schauenberg, Hofmeister of the Holy Roman Empire, asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to help their citizen Johann Fechter so that his property, which was seized on the instigation of Hans am Graben, is released again.

Burgomaster and Council of Lindau complain to Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that they did not comply with the request to send a Council delegation to the negotiation between Lindau and Count Wilhelm von Montfort in Buchhorn. They now ask the St. Gallen to send their Council delegation together with the town clerk to the newly appointed negotiation day on 6. Mai in Buchhorn.

Heinrich Schedler, Ammann of Appenzell, asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to grant Ulrich Aueler, called Tümpfler, free passage for one month. During this time, he and the Burgomaster of St. Gallen want to set a new court day in a matter between Ulrich Boppart and Ulrich Tümpfler, as Schedler cannot keep the court date set for today due to other obligations. Heinrich Schedler asks for an answer with the same messenger.

Schultheiss and Council of Bern thank Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for their efforts in settling the dispute between Schwyz and Zürich and inform them that the negotiations scheduled for 16 October have been postponed to 6 January because of the plague. They ask the St. Gallen to be in Zug with their Council delegation on the eve of this new date.

Burgomaster and Council of Ulm inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that they have received the royal and imperial right to hold a fair and a market in their city, which begins on the third Sunday after Corpus Christi and lasts 14 days. They ask the St. Gallen authorities to announce this among them and in their surroundings. In addition, a horse race with a prize is held on each occasion.

Statthalter and Council of Appenzell ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to send an envoy to a court day, which is to take place on the coming Wednesday, 1 June, in Feldkirch. If possible, the envoy should be the former Burgomaster Konrad Hör.

Wolfhart der Ältere von Brandis, Freiherr, bailiff of Feldkirch, asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to help his serf Heinrich Signer vom Eschnerberg so that the debts for two oxen sold to a citizen of St. Gallen are paid to him.

King Friedrich III. commands the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to issue a certified copy of an open letter from the King to Appenzell to the country people of Appenzell and to inform him subsequently exactly when this has been done.

Statthalter and Council of Appenzell confirm to Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that the St. Gallen citizen Hans Streiff sold silver to the Appenzell countryman Hans Mettler for 14 gulden and lawfully bought it back for the same sum.

Ammann and Council of Feldkirch send to Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen the documents concerning a dispute between several citizens of Feldkirch over the inheritance of the deceased surgeon Master Hans. The people of Feldkirch ask the people of St. Gallen in writing for legal advice for the pronouncement of the judgment.

Count Ulrich von Helfenstein the Elder asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to have a vineyard, which was occupied by citizens of St. Gallen, specifically by a Lumbrich, returned to Ulrich Knopf, son of Benz Knopf and heir of his mother Greta von Heisterkirch. Should the citizens of St. Gallen not agree to this, Count Ulrich asks for a court day and free passage for the representatives of Ulrich Knopf. Count Ulrich asks for a reply with the same messenger.

Ammann, Geschworene and Landleute of the courts of Seewis and Klosters ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to mediate in their dispute with the brothers Count Heinrich and Count Ulrich von Montfort-Tettnang.
Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen speak out to Ravensburg against the recoinage of inferior Bohemian coins.
Hans von Watt writes to the bailiffs, saying that he has not yet received the fifty gulden promised to him from the Zurzach market, and asks for the matter to be settled.

In representation of his father, Wolfhart the Younger von Brandis, Statthalter of the bailiwick of Feldkirch, asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen, in the matter of the von Höchst, to await the return of his father from Bern. He will meanwhile, however, try to settle the matter amicably with the von Höchst.

The Schultheiss and Council of Wil request, on behalf of Wolfgang Kotz, the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to ensure that Bartholome Harwer, son of a citizen of St. Gallen, pays a fine of ten schillings. Kotz had stood surety for this fine debt of Harwer towards Rudolf Seiler, the bailiff and fine collector of the abbot. The surety wishes to prevent having to take over the payment of the fine, as he himself is in straitened circumstances.

Burgomaster and Council of Lindau ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to restrain their citizen, the bell founder Master Ulrich, to finally pass a judgment in the dispute between the inhabitants of Unterreitnau and the bell founder Michael Glarer, citizen of Lindau. The Lindauers ask for a written answer with the messenger.

Burgomaster and Council of Lindau summarize the statements made in connection with the dispute between the residents of Unterreitnau and Michael Glarer over a new church bell and ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to inform them in writing of the judgment of bell-caster Master Ulrich or to send him to Lindau on 4 September for oral statements and a decision. The Lindauers ask for a written answer with the messenger.

Burgomaster and Council of Lindau ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to compel the widow of Ulrich Grabherr von Lustenau, who is a citizen of St. Gallen, to pay outstanding taxes of three gulden from her deceased husband, who was a citizen of Lindau.

The Werkmeister and Council of Chur inform the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that they have heard that Eglolf von Rorschach, the Elder, a citizen of St. Gallen, accuses the people of Chur for unknown reasons. They ask the people of St. Gallen to see to it with Eglolf von Rorschach that he leave them undisturbed. Otherwise, they would be glad to come to St. Gallen for a hearing. The people of Chur ask for a written answer with the messenger.

Wolfhart der Ältere von Brandis, bailiff of Feldkirch, informs the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that he has appointed a negotiation for 7 January in Höchst regarding the dispute between the inhabitants of Rheineck and the court servants of Höchst over a meadow. He asks the St. Gallen to send a council delegation to the negotiation.

Wolfhart der Ältere von Brandis, bailiff of Feldkirch, informs the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that, owing to the dispute between the citizen of St. Gallen Eberhard von Ramschwag and Hans von Ems, he has appointed a court day in Feldkirch for 12 March and promises the parties safe conduct for it. He asks for a written confirmation.
Burgomaster and Council of Lindau ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to better protect their merchants, who went to St. Gallen for the fair of 9 May, from their enemies in the Neckertal.

Burgomaster and Council of Schaffhausen request, on behalf of their Kantengiesser Heinrich Klob and his stepsons Peter Nünangster and Hans Klinger, Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to set a negotiation between Heinrich Klob and the city of Überlingen. The Schaffhausen authorities ask the St. Gallen authorities for a written reply with the same messenger.

Burgomaster and Council of Schaffhausen thank Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for agreeing to mediate the dispute between the city of Überlingen and Heinrich Klob, and ask them to settle it as soon as possible.

Ammann and Council of Feldkirch inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that a deadly cattle plague has broken out at Eschnerberg and in the Rheintal and that affected animals may have been sold to St. Gallen. The Feldkirch authorities have forbidden their butchers to buy cattle from the affected area.

King Friedrich III. informs the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that Jakob, Truchsess von Waldburg and Landvogt in Schwaben, will come to St. Gallen, and commands the citizens of St. Gallen to give belief to Jakob's statements as to his own.

King Friedrich III. commands the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to grant faith to Jakob, Truchsess von Waldburg and Landvogt in Schwaben, who comes to St. Gallen because of the dispute between Eberhard von Ramschwag and Hans von Ems, as to himself.

Burgomaster and Council of Lindau inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen, in response to their inquiry, that the King, according to a letter from Rösch von Überlingen ten days old, was still in Frankfurt, but that it could not be gathered from this letter when and where the King wished to travel next.

Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen, in response to their inquiry, that they have learned from their returning council colleagues that King Friedrich III. is to depart from Frankfurt for Friedberg on 13 August and subsequently proceed along the Rhine to Worms, Speyer and Strassburg and into the Breisgau. They do not know whether the King has departed in the meantime, but they promise to inform the St. Gallen authorities if they should learn anything.

Bishop Heinrich of Konstanz asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to bring their people to make a statement regarding timber offenses in his forests in the vicinity of Arbon, so that he does not have to summon them judicially, which he would do reluctantly. He asks for a reply.

Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to obtain information about the time of death of Hans Neukomm, so that the disputes over the inheritance of the brothers Hans and Ulrich Neukomm between Heini Hör, citizen of St. Gallen, his sister and brother, and Konrad Zollikofer, citizen of Konstanz, can be settled. The people of Konstanz ask for a written answer with the messenger.

Ammann, Rechtsprecher and the gemeinen Hofleute of Berneck ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for a court day on which a decision is to be made regarding cattle transit rights on the meadow of Tudeler. The Berneckers ask for a reply.

Burgomaster and Council of Lindau ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to bring their citizens to a point where they do not attack Hans Melli, called Ätti von Buchen. Salt was stolen from him on the fair of 28 October by the St. Gallen citizen Hans Baumann, called Nänger von Obersteinach, a friend of the citizens of St. Gallen. On account of the accusation of theft against Baumann, citizens of St. Gallen have declared enmity against Hans Melli. The Lindauers ask for a written answer.

Wolfhart von Brandis, bailiff of Feldkirch, promises the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that, in the case of Hans Müller, who has been accused by Juckin before the Landgericht in Konstanz, he will endeavor to have the court proceedings transferred to the Hofgericht in Höchst, but rejects the proposal to hold the proceedings in St. Gallen.

Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that they are advocating with the bailiffs of the Landgericht that the proceedings concerning several citizens of St. Gallen not be conducted before they had exchanged views with one another. A postponement also applies to a woman named Tannermann.

Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen once again to speak with their fellow citizen Heini Hör, so that he either testifies in the dispute with the citizen of Konstanz Konrad Zollikofer over the inheritance of the deceased son of Hans Neukomm, or lets the matter rest.

Wolfhart der Ältere von Brandis, bailiff of Feldkirch, asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to ensure that Helbok, who was innocently taken prisoner by the Ammann, the two Giger, and the son of Hans Müller of St. Margrethen-Höchst, is released again. If this does not happen, he says that he must report the incident to the King. He asks for a written answer with the messenger.

Wolfhart der Ältere von Brandis, bailiff of Feldkirch, asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to hand over Helbok, who was captured in the judicial territory of his Austrian lordship, and promises to keep him available for a court hearing. He asks for a written answer with the messenger.

Hans von Breitenlandenberg informs the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that the abbot of the Benedictine monastery of St. Gallen agrees to a court day in a matter between him and the city, and asks for written notification of whether the city is still interested in it and when and where it is to be held.

After the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen have informed Hans von Breitenlandenberg that they wish to hold the court day with the Abbot of St. Gallen in St. Gallen, Hans von Breitenlandenberg informs the citizens of St. Gallen that the Abbot agrees to this and proposes the 13. Mai as the date.

Ammann and Council in the Bregenzerwald inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that they are willing to pay Klara von Ramschwag the interest from their territory as soon as she provides two or four sureties from Dornbirn as security. They ask for a written answer.

Hans von Breitenlandenberg informs the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that the Abbot of St. Gallen will not attend the promised court day on 13 May, as his retinue cannot be present. He asks for forgiveness that the notification is made so late.

Heinrich von Hewen, Bishop of Konstanz, asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to provide him with a Council delegation to support him at a court day with Stickel von Konstanz before Landvogt Jakob Truchsess von Waldburg on 29 May in Bregenz.

Burgomaster and Council of Lindau ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to provide them again with a Council delegation for support for a court day in Isny on 2 July. A first court day did not take place, as the opposing party had not appeared on the court day and considered the Landvogt to be biased, which is why the King had appointed a new judge, namely the Bishop of Augsburg.

Burgomaster and Council of Lindau write to Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen: Johann Norder, a household member of Balgach who was subject to the jurisdiction of the Abbess of Lindau, got into a dispute with his sister and his brother-in-law Klaus Schneider before the court of Balgach. On a court day at the abbey's palace, it was decided that Norder had lost the dispute and that it should be settled. However, Norder evaded the jurisdiction of the Abbess by accepting the citizenship of St. Gallen, whereupon he was placed under the third ban by the Abbess, from which he was again released by Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen. Burgomaster and Council of Lindau ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to endeavor to have their citizen Johann Norder from Balgach appear before the court in Konstanz, so that these disputes can be heard. They ask for a written answer with the messenger.

Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz urge Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to send a Council delegation to Konstanz regarding Konrad Peyer and several servants imprisoned in Berneck, so that this matter can be handled orally rather than in writing. Should Konstanz and St. Gallen fail to reach an agreement, the Berneckers are to proceed as is lawful.

Burgomaster and Council of Ravensburg inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that the Imperial Cities in Schwaben were unable to reach an agreement in the dispute between Lindau and Anna Finstertaler and how to proceed. Some Imperial Cities do not want to provide Lindau with support before the Reichskammergericht. Konstanz sent a Council delegation to the King and asks that the other Imperial Cities share in the costs. All of this is to be discussed again in Ravensburg on 2 December.
Hans von Breitenlandenberg asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to make a Council delegation available to him in Winterthur on 16 December.

Ammann and Council in the Bregenzerwald reply to Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen regarding a letter concerning Hans Steinli and his wife with respect to a dispute over an inheritance with local residents. The matter is to be heard on 27 February, whereby Hans Steinli and his wife may bring support. They ask for a reply with the messenger.

Ammann and Hofleute of Berneck ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for advice in settling a dispute in Marbach between Berneckers and a man from Lustenau on the one hand, and several Kriessern and a citizen of Altstätten on the other. A Bernecker named Kern was wounded, and a brawl arose, so that Klara von Ramschwag had to provide justice.

Anton Schenk von Landegg, bailiff of Bischofszell, asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to ensure that the citizen of St. Gallen Konrad Künzli von Brüewil, together with his kin, who are also citizens of St. Gallen and who have attacked a poor man called Brüewiler and a tenant of Anton Schenk and of Walter von Andwil, present themselves. As had been promised by the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen.

Dorothea von Altstätten replies to the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen, who have written to her regarding the warlike actions, that she will speak with her people so that they will not interfere in the ongoing dispute of the St. Gallen.

Marquard Brisacher informs the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that the dispute between the citizen of St. Gallen Ulrich Engler and Pulsterholz should be adjudicated before the court of the Bishop of Konstanz, as the dispute took place in Bischofszell, and furthermore Egli Weber, who belongs to the abbot of St. Gallen, was involved. If this proposal does not suit the people of St. Gallen, Pulsterholz is willing to appear before the Council of St. Gallen, however under the condition that Egli Weber also appears. Brisacher asks for a notification of what would suit the people of St. Gallen.

Ammann, Rechtssprecher and Hofleute of Berneck ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for advice on how two Eigenleute of Merk von Ems, Hofleute of Berneck, who have accepted the citizenship of St. Gallen together with them, should conduct themselves so that they do not come into conflict with their lord.

Ammann and Council of Bregenz inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that the servants who are loitering in Hard, Lauterach and elsewhere do not harbor hostility towards the St. Gallen citizens, but that they were nevertheless requested by the bailiff of Bregenz to move on.
Ammann and Council of Schwyz request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to hand over to Werner Stocker, the bearer of this letter, the 1600 gulden that Schwyz has borrowed from St. Gallen.

Burgomaster and Council of Lindau inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that a ship with mercenaries is on the Bodensee, but its destination is unknown to them. In an accompanying letter, Burgomaster and Council of Lindau ask to be informed as soon as Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen learn anything new about the French and foreign people (Armagnacs) who are roaming in the Klettgau and have inflicted a defeat on the Confederates.

Burgomaster and Council of Lindau inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that a ship with mercenaries is on the Bodensee, but its destination is unknown to them. In an accompanying letter, Burgomaster and Council of Lindau ask to be informed as soon as Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen learn anything new about the French and Welsche people (Armagnacs) who are roaming in the Klettgau and have inflicted a defeat on the Confederates.

Burgomaster and Council of Überlingen inform Truchsess Jakob von Waldburg, Landvogt in Schwaben, that at his request they will keep the negotiation concerning the St. Gallen citizen Johann Gerster, taken prisoner by them, in abeyance until 29 September.

King Friedrich III. informs the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that they are to provide 12 horsemen, including crossbowmen, to combat the Armagnacs, who are to assemble in Strassburg on 16 October.

Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to send a Council delegation to Konstanz on 2 October, so that it can consult the following day with other delegations on how to proceed in the present, difficult situation.

King Friedrich III. informs all his subjects that he has appointed Pfalzgraf Ludwig IV. bei Rhein, Elector of the Palatinate and Duke of Bayern, as supreme commander of the Imperial levy against the Armagnacs. Whoever does not comply with the orders of the supreme commander will be severely punished.

Hans Wilhelm von Friedingen, bailiff of Bregenz, informs the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that he has heard nothing about several Bregenz residents having stolen horses from Hans Gimmel, a poor man of the St. Gallen citizen Dorothea von Altstätten, or that people from Balgach, also citizens of St. Gallen, would still owe money for grain. He says that he will, however, inquire into these matters.

Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that they will advocate before the Landgericht that the Council members summoned by the court because of Zerahoch are to be questioned in St. Gallen.

Ammann and Council of Feldkirch reply to Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to the accusation of the St. Gallen citizens that several of them had been robbed, that it is not they, but their lordship that is at war. But they are ready to investigate injustices, as is customary.
Duke Albrecht von Österreich grants a twelve-member St. Gallen delegation safe conduct until 2 February and orders all his subjects to protect this right of safe conduct.

Burgomaster and Council of Überlingen inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that they have not confiscated the property of the St. Gallen citizen Anna Gerster. The disputed property fell to the city according to city law after the death of the mother of Anna's stepson, who is a citizen of Überlingen and is under guardianship here. Hans Gerster, the father of the child and Anna Gerster's husband, was never in possession of this property, and Anna also has no claim. Burgomaster and Council of Überlingen invite Anna Gerster to a court day on 27 January to clarify the matter. The Überlingen authorities request a written reply with the messenger.

Anton Schenk von Landegg, bailiff of Bischofszell, informs the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that he has opened a letter from Wil to the citizens of St. Gallen, and asks them not to take this ill.

The bailiff, Ammann and Council of Bregenz, to whom the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen had written regarding the capture of several citizens of St. Gallen on Lake Constance and their transfer to Bregenz, and had requested safe conduct, reply to the St. Gallens that the Bregenzers are ready to grant the St. Gallens safe conduct to Bregenz before their gracious lordship. If this is not to their liking, the St. Gallens could be released for a certain period against surety or a payment of money.

The bailiff, Ammann and Council of Bregenz inform the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that the citizens of St. Gallen in Bregenz may go about undisturbed, although citizens of St. Gallen were involved in the attack of the Confederates on Hard. The condition, however, is that the citizens of St. Gallen do not let anything come to the enemies of Bregenz.

Albrecht Tumb von Neuburg informs the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that his son and his wife were robbed without cause by the Appenzellers and the Glarners, which surprises him, since his daughter-in-law and her mother are connected with the St. Gallers. He therefore asks the St. Gallers to intervene on their behalf. He asks for a written answer.

Duke Albrecht von Österreich has invited the Bishops of Augsburg and Konstanz, the Society of the Georgenschild and other knightly orders as well as several Imperial cities for 11 April and asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to send a Council delegation to him at Mengen for 13 April.

Anton Schenk von Landegg, bailiff of Bischofszell, asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to render a judgment, or to have one rendered by others, in a dispute between citizens of St. Gallen, in place of Lienhart Brühwiler, who is biased. Furthermore, he informs them that a military campaign will pass between St. Gallen and Arbon, and advises them to inform the exiles there that they should secure their movable property and livestock, as they would otherwise likely be plundered.

Bailiff, Ammann and Council of Arbon reply to a letter from Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen, saying that they have, on the order of the Bishop of Konstanz, taken captive an Eigenmann and other men and brought them to Arbon.

Ammann and the Hofleute of Lustenau, as citizens of St. Gallen, address the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen and ask for advice and help, as they were attacked and damaged by the Appenzellers without cause, and offer to settle any disputes with them before the Council of St. Gallen. The people of Lustenau ask for a written answer with the messenger.

Ammann and Council of Altstätten inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that the people of Kunigunde Tumb may come to Altstätten, provided they swear to the Appenzellers, which the citizens of Altstätten also did on the orders of the Appenzellers.

Ludwig, a piper, asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that he, together with his two new journeymen, be taken into the service of the city, as had been agreed with him and his previous journeymen. He asks for an answer.

Duke Albrecht von Österreich asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for the names of the four citizens of St. Gallen for whom he is to issue a letter of introduction at the request of the St. Gallen.
Burgomaster and Council of Lindau issue a letter of recommendation for Johannes Redrer, who applies in person in St. Gallen as schoolmaster.
Bailiff, Ammann and Council of Bregenz reply to Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen, who want to send a negotiation delegation to Bregenz, that they promise this delegation safe conduct.

Albrecht von Breitenlandenberg answers the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen, who had written to him regarding a dispute with the inhabitants of Kesswil. He lets them know that he has transferred the mandate for negotiations. He asks for a reply.

Anton Schenk von Landegg, bailiff of Bischofszell, mediates in a dispute between a citizen of St. Gallen named Peter Marshüblin and a man of Konstanz named Rukli Frienherten and others. He asks the Council of St. Gallen to admonish his citizen so that he keeps the agreed peace. He asks for a written answer with the same messenger.

Ammann and Council of Altstätten answer Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen regarding their inquiry concerning Künigunde von Tumb, saying that they (Altstätten) will apply customary town and country law. They communicate that they will shortly send an embassy for consultation.

Burgomaster and Council of Überlingen answer Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen regarding a letter of the St. Gallen concerning the prisoner named Seger. The St. Gallen are to travel to Überlingen for the trial, so that the accused may be sentenced to death, which his peers may publicly see.

Hans von Gänserndorf, chamberlain of Duke Albrecht von Österreich, complains to the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that the Hauptmann Heuschreiber and other citizens and mercenaries of St. Gallen had taken his father-in-law Walter von Schönenbühl, who had been travelling by ship to Konstanz in a matter of the Duke, prisoner. He asks for the release of the prisoner, otherwise he must file a complaint with the Duke. He asks for an answer with the same messenger.

The Council of Amberg asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to intervene on behalf of their citizen Heinrich Heiden. False rumors are being spread about him by the Lords of Ems and others. They also ask the St. Gallen authorities, in the name of their lord, the Palatine, to write to the Lords of Ems and to ask them, as well as Heinrich and Walter von Ramschwag, for moderation.

Wolfhard von Brandis der Ältere asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to provide him with envoys to support him in a negotiation with the Bernese in Baden. The St. Gallen envoys are to arrive at the inn on the eve of the negotiation of 1 June.

Schultheiss and Council of Wil inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that the citizens of St. Gallen, Strub von Züberwangen, had seized linen from the Wiler council member Heinrich Wetzel. They ask the St. Gallen authorities to instruct the Strub family to return their (Wiler) citizen's property. Wil asks for a reply.

Ammann and Council of Appenzell inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen about a court day on 15. February in Altstätten, at which a dispute from Abtwil is to be heard. The Appenzellers ask the St. Gallen to send them Junker Konrad von Andwil, their Council colleague, for support, as he is already familiar with the matter.

Ammann and Council of Appenzell complain to Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that the two St. Gallen priests Hans Rüti and Hans Särri, citizens of St. Gallen, want to bring the Appenzell countrymen Schmid von Goldach, Hans Pütinger, and a usurer before the ecclesiastical court over interest disputes. They ask the St. Gallen authorities to admonish their citizens and propose that the matter be adjudicated before their own court.
Schultheiss and Council of Rapperswil request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to mediate in an inheritance dispute between Klaus Halder and the children of von Langenhard.

Schultheiss and Council of Wil request, on behalf of their resident Hans Langenhard, Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to support them in a dispute between Klaus Halder von Mollenberg and the children of Jakob von Langenhard.
Heinrich Payer asks his brother-in-law, the St. Gallen Burgomaster Heinrich Zwick, to lend him money.

Ammann and Council of Appenzell request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to convene a town meeting on 26 December 1448, as they (Appenzell) have something to negotiate with the St. Gallen citizens. Furthermore, they request the St. Gallen citizens not to place the widow of their deceased countryman Hans Schnagg under guardianship before they have spoken about it. The Appenzell citizens request a written reply with the same messenger.
Ammann and Hofleute of Lustenau ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for patience, as they (Lustenau) at the moment cannot pay the taxes owed.

Ammann and Council of Schwyz send Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen 100 gulden of due interest. 20 further gulden, which will soon be due, they (the Schwyzers) will bring to them (the St. Galleners) to the (St. Gallen) Burgomaster for a negotiation on 22 June in Uznach. The Schwyzers ask for a receipt.

Duke Albrecht von Österreich informs the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen about an attack by the Fulacher and Roggwiler on the castle of his advisor Bilgeri von Heudorf and asks them to support him in his efforts to maintain peace. The Fulacher brothers retake the castle Laufen from Bilgeri, after he had occupied it in 1448 on the basis of alleged inheritance claims.

Heinrich, Bishop of Konstanz, asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to support him in a negotiation on 28 July in Lindau with Rudolf von Underwegen by sending a delegation of the Council. They are to assemble on the Saturday before the negotiation at the episcopal castle in Arbon.

The Werkmeister and Council of Chur request the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to support them with a Council delegation in a negotiation on 28 July in Lindau with Rudolf von Underwegen. They are to assemble the evening before at the inn.

Friedrich, Römischer König and Herzog von Österreich, informs the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that he has had to postpone his journey to Rome, in which citizens of St. Gallen would also participate. The reason for this is a plague, which is why the Pope is not in Rome. The King tells the citizens of St. Gallen that he will inform them when he will set out for Rome.

Ursula Schenk asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for information about her children, as Ulrich Truchsess has given up the bailiwick over her children and she has long heard nothing in this matter.

Ammann and Council of Schwyz request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to support them in a dispute. The father of the priest Johannes Senn had debts to the St. Gallen citizen Fridpolt, whereupon Fridpolt had confiscated Senn's house. Schwyz asks St. Gallen to speak with Fridpolt to obtain a deferral of repayment.

Friedrich, Archbishop of Salzburg and Legate of the Pope, Silvester, Bishop of Chiemsee, Albrecht, Pfalzgraf bei Rhein, Duke of Bayern and Count of Vohburg, as well as Hans von Neidberg and Meister Ulrich Rieder inform the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that the King invites to a Diet on 12 April in München. The citizens of St. Gallen are to send a Council delegation and thereby help to restore peace and unity in the Empire. A royal letter of safe conduct is enclosed.

Johannes Widenbach sends Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen information from the Imperial Diet in München. The Princes of Mainz, Brandenburg, Niederbaden and Württemberg had sent only four messengers, whereby no agreement could be found on the first day. He does not yet know whether an agreement will come about, as the cities are not willing to renounce freedoms.

Several Imperial cities, which are involved in the pledge of the Lordship of Hohenberg, describe to the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen the events concerning the dispute with the Dukes Ernst and Friedrich of Österreich, which arose over the pledge of the Lordship of Hohenberg. They ask that no support be given to the Dukes or their helpers, and expect a written answer with the messenger.
Ammann and Council of Appenzell inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that they (Appenzell) have admitted Frau Küngold von Altstätten into their Landrecht.
Burgomaster and Council of Bopfingen recommend to Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen Rudolf Aich, who had stayed with them and behaved according to the norm.

Draft of a complaint from the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to Jakob Truchsess von Waldburg, Landvogt, that he should ensure that their (St. Gallen) citizen Wilhelm Ringgli is refunded his shipment of lard. Ringgli had been on his way to the market in Konstanz when his (Jakob Truchsess von Waldburg's) men had attacked him. The St. Gallen ask for a written answer with the messenger.

Margareta von Heidelberg grants her husband Liebhard Ledergerber power of attorney, as she herself cannot attend the court day regarding disputes concerning the purchase of Rorschach between them (the spouses) and the abbot and convent of the Benedictine monastery of St. Gallen.

Duke Albrecht von Österreich asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for a delegation that is to support him in a negotiation on 5 October in Konstanz against Jobst von Hornstein. The delegation is to arrive in Konstanz on the eve for a preliminary discussion.

Rudolf Locher von Hagenbuch, mercenary in Rottweil, asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to forgive him the manslaughter he committed in St. Gallen years ago, after the fine has been paid, and to let him back into the city. He asks for a written answer.

Burgomaster and Council of Radolfzell inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that they (Radolfzell) will no longer pursue the St. Gallen Ruedi Fischer and Ruedi Baumann for past matters. However, they assume that nothing of the sort will happen in the future.

Ammann and Council of Appenzell summon Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to a court hearing concerning the matter of Ulrich von Steig to Gossau on 16 December. The Appenzellers have also informed the abbot of the Benedictine monastery of St. Gallen and ask for notification if the St. Gallen cannot attend the date.

Heinrich Schlosser from Bern complains to the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that Ulrich Gelter, a citizen of St. Gallen, has spread the lie in Nürnberg that he (Gelter) had seen him (Schlosser) hanged on the gallows in Baden. Schlosser asks the people of St. Gallen to reprimand Gelter. He asks for a written answer.

Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that the scheduled negotiation in the dispute concerning the citizens of St. Gallen Hans Mötteli and Peter Gubser can take place as planned. Hans Mötteli would have safe conduct in the city of Konstanz for 14 days.

Ammann and Council of Appenzell ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to send a delegation of two men to the court proceedings of Ulrich von Steig, just as they themselves and the abbot of the Benedictine monastery of St. Gallen would also do. They ask for a written answer with the messenger.

Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen about the course of the negotiation with the citizen of St. Gallen Ulrich Särri and about the question of whether Hans Mötteli and his wife have to issue a receipt or not. Zürich has offered to take up the matter, for which Konstanz is grateful.

Burgomaster and Council of Basel inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that the cause of the verbal outbursts in St. Gallen against them (the Basel authorities) had been a very protracted dispute between Ulrich Schmitter, a citizen of Basel, and his wife on the one hand, and Margarethe von Kilchen on the other. They describe the dispute and ask St. Gallen to report to them if anything should happen again in St. Gallen in this connection.

Kaspar von Breitenlandenberg, abbot of the Benedictine monastery of St. Gallen, informs the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that he cannot grant any further delay in the dispute between Heinrich Schmid von Waldkirch and the Loppacher family and has set the hearing for 22 February.

Ammann and Council of Appenzell inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen about a dispute between Hermann Grunder, Klaus Heer and Hans Riemer, Appenzell countrymen, and Heinrich Maier of Oberdorf, a citizen of St. Gallen, over seven Rhenish gulden. They ask them (the St. Gallen authorities) to persuade their citizen to abide by the court judgment passed and to pay his debts. They ask for a written reply with the messenger.

Ammann and Council of Schwyz inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that at the last meeting of the Confederates in Luzern, at which the abbot of the Benedictine monastery of St. Gallen had also been present, it was discussed to hold a meeting in St. Gallen on 1. August. The subject of negotiation is the settlement of the conflict between the monastery and the city of St. Gallen with the involvement of Luzern, Schwyz and Glarus. The abbot has already agreed. They ask for a written answer with the messenger and for safe conduct for the abbot's scribe.

Heinrich Feuerstein, Ammann in the Hinteren Bregenzerwald, asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for help in an inheritance matter. A deceased man named Wölfli, a citizen of the Hinteren Bregenzerwald, had triggered the inheritance of his wife Älli, daughter of Heinz Schnell, also from the Hinteren Bregenzerwald. Now Feuerstein asks the St. Gallen authorities to assist the widow in the return of her inheritance.

Hans Betschart of St. Gallen reports to the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that he, together with several family members, had been taken prisoner by Count Heinrich von Tengen on the way to Stockach, and that a hearing has now been set for 8 August in Stockach. He asks St. Gallen to send an embassy to support him.

Hans von Watt complains to the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that much injustice has been done to him, among other things by the Council itself. Among other things, he says that he was driven out of his house, and his wife was insulted. He asks the Burgomaster and Council to support him.

Schultheiss and Council of Wil inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that Konrad Bauer, parish priest of Niederbüren and sworn member of Wil, having been threatened by Jäckli Ambühl and citizens of St. Gallen while he was proclaiming something on behalf of the Hofammann. They ask the St. Gallen authorities to ensure Bauer's safety, who is willing to answer for accusations. They also ask for a written reply with the messenger.

Rudolf von Landenberg von Greifensee informs the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that one of their citizens would have had a dispute with him. Since this dispute would have begun before this citizen of St. Gallen had become a citizen, the authorities of St. Gallen would not be responsible. Rudolf von Landenberg asks St. Gallen to no longer concern itself with the matter.

Burgomaster and Council of Wangen inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that, despite the invitation from St. Gallen, they will not send a delegation to a negotiation in St. Gallen on 3 October, because the abbot of the Benedictine monastery of St. Gallen, their lord, has not requested them to do so.

The cities of the Schwäbischen Städtebundes ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to send a delegation of the Council to support the cities on 12 October at a negotiation in Diessenhofen, to which Duke Albrecht von Österreich has invited the cities of Schaffhausen and Rottweil.

Burgomaster and Council of Ulm request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to support with advice and action the merchants from Ulm and other cities around Lake Constance who wish to visit the fair on St. Gall's Day in St. Gallen against hostile attacks.

Ammann and Council of Appenzell inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that Hans Künzler of Kesswil has become their countryman. They ask that he be treated like all their other countrymen. If anyone has anything to bring against him, the person concerned should turn to their court.

Burgomaster and Council of Ulm inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen about a dispute and ask for their opinion. Rudolf Muntprat of Ravensburg and Georg Ehinger, citizens of Ulm, had been taken prisoner by Heinrich von Isenburg the Younger, and in the course of protracted negotiations for their release they had proposed several persons as judges, which Heinrich von Isenburg had not wanted to accept. They ask St. Gallen not to give credence to any statements against them, and for a written answer with the messenger.

Burgomaster and Council of Radolfzell ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for legal assistance. Their former Burgomaster Ital Dietrich Vogt is to appear together with Ulrich Blarer the Younger of Konstanz before the abbot of the Benedictine monastery of St. Gallen as a commissioner of the King. They ask the St. Gallen authorities to send a Council delegation on 10 December for support.

Anton Schenk von Landegg, bailiff of Bischofszell, reports to the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that, on the order of his lord, he has taken the widow and the daughter of Thomas Schweizer prisoner in Konstanz. St. Gallen is to write to his lord in Konstanz in order to obtain more information in this matter.

Burgomaster and Council of Ulm report to Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that they have announced a new court hearing in Konstanz in the matter of the friends and citizens of Ulm taken prisoner by Hans Rechberg and Heinrich von Isenburg. They ask the St. Gallen to send them a Council delegation for support on 16 January.

Burgomaster and Council of Zürich inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that they are to hold a court hearing concerning Markgraf Wilhelm von Hochberg with Herzog Sigismund von Österreich in Konstanz, and ask St. Gallen to send a delegation on 2 February to support them.
