Rudolf Beck the scribe asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen, after he had been brought before the city court, to assure him of safe conduct for one month, so that he may come into the city and settle his affairs to the benefit of all parties concerned. He asks for a reply to be sent to his wife or to his daughter.

Heinrich IV. von Hewen, Bishop of Konstanz, informs the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that he will shortly send envoys to St. Gallen to inform them in the matter of the widow of Thomas Schweizer and her daughter.

Ammann and Council of Arbon inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that the Arbon citizen Margaretha Buchmüller had been brought before the court of Burkhard Schenk in Roggwil by the St. Gallen citizen Adelheid Uhler of Uttwil, although she had done nothing to be blamed for. Arbon asks St. Gallen to convince their citizen to drop the matter. Should Margaretha Buchmüller have done anything to be blamed for, they would bring her before their own court, as had been customary between them in good friendship until now.

Heinrich IV. von Hewen, Bishop of Konstanz, asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen, in the matter of the great harm which the citizen of St. Gallen Hans Mötteli has caused, what he should undertake and whether they would proceed against Mötteli, since he is a citizen of St. Gallen. He asks for a written answer with the messenger.

Heinrich IV. von Hewen, Bishop of Konstanz, informs the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that what Hans Mötteli had told them and to which they would refer in a letter is not correct. Mötteli had not yet chosen the legal path against him, but had raided the castle of Arbon by night and fog. The Bishop repeats his request that he and the citizens of St. Gallen should exchange views on further proceedings. He asks for a written answer with the messenger.

Burgomaster and Council of Wangen warn Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that about 30 horsemen and as many foot soldiers would be waiting on the Ruggburg until merchants pass by, whom they would then rob. Wangen asks St. Gallen to warn everyone.

Burgomaster and Council of Schaffhausen inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that they have been invited to a negotiation with Duke Sigismund of Österreich in Konstanz on 25 May. They ask St. Gallen to support them with a Council delegation. They ask for a written answer with the messenger.

Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen ask Heinrich IV. von Hewen, Bishop of Konstanz, to settle the conflict between their citizen Hans Mötteli and him, the Bishop, before the court of the Emperor or the Landgericht of Jakob Truchsess von Waldburg, after the Bishop had not accepted the towns as arbitral instances. They ask for a written answer with the messenger.

Konrad Stüdli, priest, who has taken up a benefice in the Lordship of Landsberg in Alsace after his departure from St. Gallen four years ago, reports to the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen about ill will. Among other things, the rumor is being spread that he is not a priest and that he was forbidden in St. Gallen from exercising his office. Since he lost his letter of ordination in the Armagnac Wars and he suffers under insults, he asks the people of St. Gallen for the issuance of a sealed letter in his favor.

Freiherr Wolfhart von Brandis der Ältere recommends to the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen his Eigenmann Jakob Vosch, at the latter's request, for admission to the citizenship of St. Gallen. As a condition, Brandis stipulates that this must not diminish his rights.

Burgomaster and Council of Lindau request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to send a Council delegation to a negotiation on 20 June, which they are to have in Buchhorn with Count Ulrich von Montfort, Lord of Tettnang, in their support.

Anton Schenk von Landegg, bailiff of Bischofszell, informs his uncle, the St. Gallen Burgomaster Ulrich Särri, that the court hearing in Bischofszell against Ruedi Mayer, which he had set, cannot take place on the appointed day. The hearing between Strub and Müller, however, would take place as planned. Schenk von Landegg asks that the persons involved in St. Gallen be informed about this.

Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that they, as before, are concerned about the high price of meat. The recent negotiations to avoid inflation had remained without result, the content of which is noted in the attached slip (attachment lost). Konstanz now invites to a new negotiation on 24 July. St. Gallen is to discuss the problem in the Councils beforehand and send a Council delegation to the negotiation in Konstanz.

Heinrich IV. von Hewen, Bishop of Konstanz, informs the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that he cannot grant any delay for the payment of 200 gulden promised by the two Burgomasters of St. Gallen for 25 July in connection with Frau Schweizer and her child. He expects the settlement within eight days. Furthermore, he will soon answer the St. Gallen regarding the matter of Herr Mötteli.

Heinrich IV. von Hewen, Bishop of Konstanz, writes to the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen regarding their citizen Hans Mötteli and states that he fears no court proceedings with Mötteli or St. Gallen if they would continue to protect and support their citizen. The Bishop asks for a written answer with the messenger.

Burgomaster and Council of Lindau inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that some citizens of St. Gallen intend to come to Lindau for a shooting festival to maintain fellowship and joy, which they find pleasing. However, the weather is now too bad, so that the festival must be postponed. They ask the citizens of St. Gallen to inform their shooting companions so that they would come later.

Burgomaster and Council of Ulm inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen in detail about the protracted negotiations concerning the capture of Rudolf Muntprat of Ravensburg and Georg Ehinger, citizen of Ulm, by Hans von Rechberg as well as Heinrich von Isenburg the Younger. The Ulm side asks the St. Gallen side not to give credence to any statements against them, but to help them and in particular not to grant Heinrich von Geroldseck, Hans von Rechberg, and Heinrich Isenburg any stay or escort. Furthermore, they ask for a written answer with the messenger.

Johannes Henseler, town clerk of Aarau, complains to the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that all kinds of rumors are being spread about him and his family, and although he had already earlier requested a correction in St. Gallen, members of the Council had publicly spoken ill of him. He requests a hearing in St. Gallen with safe conduct for the defense of his honor. In addition, he requests a written answer.

Liebhard Ledergerber, citizen of St. Gallen, asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to make the former Burgomaster Konrad Hör available to him for support in a negotiation with the abbot of the Benedictine monastery of St. Gallen in Bischofszell. If the latter cannot come, he asks for a representative of Hör.

Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that they have acted in an inheritance dispute according to the will of the St. Gallen and have ensured that Ulrich Schüber, a pensioner in the Konstanz hospital, will no longer invoke the ecclesiastical court.

Brother Wilhelm Rosslauf, Kaplan, recommends Heinrich Sigg, a young, approximately 30-year-old Mönch in the Predigerkloster in Konstanz, to the Burgomaster and Council in St. Gallen for a life annuity of 12 gulden for 120 gulden. Rosslauf asks the St. Gallen authorities to issue a letter to Sigg, as to himself and his sister, to have this given to a messenger to Konstanz, to whom the 120 Rhenish gulden would then be handed over.

Burgomaster and Council of Lindau inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen about a fishing regulation for Lent, which they have drawn up with their lordship of Bregenz as well as Count Hugo von Montfort, lord of Rothenfels. They ask St. Gallen to proclaim this regulation to their fishermen and to enforce it.

Ammann and Council of Bregenz inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen about a fishing regulation for Lent, which they have drawn up with their lordship as well as Count Hugo von Montfort, Lord of Rotenfels, and with the Burgomaster and Council of Lindau. They ask St. Gallen to proclaim this regulation to their fishermen and to enforce it.

Burgomaster and Council of Zürich inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that they have attacked several servants who had detained and robbed travellers in their County of Kyburg, after these delinquents had escaped from their county. The people of Winterthur have now set a court day at short notice, which they unfortunately announced late. The people of Zürich ask the people of St. Gallen to send a delegation of the Council to the proceedings in Winterthur to support them.

As advocates of the Bishop of Konstanz, Nikolaus Gundelfinger, Vikar, Johannes Lidrunger, Siegler, and Sigmund vom Stein, Ritter, write to the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen, because the St. Gallen authority had issued a purchase ban for St. Gallen citizens at the Bischofszell market. The St. Gallen had later relaxed the ban for the sake of the Bishop of Konstanz, allowing the purchase of yarn but not of linen. Now the representatives of the Bishop of Konstanz ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to additionally lift the purchase ban for St. Gallen citizens of linen at the Bischofszell market. The people of Konstanz ask for a written answer with the messenger.

Ammann and Council of Arbon inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that a mediation took place before the Council of Arbon between the family Grimm and the Arboner Wilhelm Ulmann. After the negotiation, the Grimms had demanded compensation before they were willing to release Ulmann from the debt. Ulmann replied that he was ready to pay the Grimms what was appropriate according to the court judgment. The Arboners therefore ask the St. Gallen for communication of their decision.

Burgomaster and Council of Wangen inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that in the dispute between the city of Lindau and the citizen of Wangen Kaspar Schwarz, a date for negotiations has been set for 15 March. Since Lindau cannot send a Council delegation for reasons of war, they ask St. Gallen to send a Council delegation to support their citizen at the negotiations.

The bailiff and Council of Bischofszell inform the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that their citizen Ulrich Herr has a court hearing with Hans Hüniswiler in Oberuzwil on 21 March, and they ask the St. Gallen authorities to send a delegation of the Council there to support him.

Burgomaster and Council of Lindau inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that they have a court hearing with Count Ulrich von Montfort in Buchhorn on 17 July, and they ask the St. Gallen to send a Council delegation to support them.

Hans von Klingenberg, knight and Landvogt in Thurgau, informs the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that he has settled a dispute between knight Heinrich von Roggwil and Kaspar Sänger. This peace, however, was only negotiated until 24 August. He asks the citizens of St. Gallen to speak with their citizen Oppertshofer and to do everything to ensure that the peace holds. He also asks for a written report of their measures with the messenger.

Hans Brändli, bailiff of Arbon, informs the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that Peter Wetzel from Goldach and others have told him that they hold in fief a tenth of the Stifft of Konstanz, for the payment of which several citizens of St. Gallen are obliged. Brändli asks, on behalf of the tenth holders, the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to compel the tenth-liable citizens of St. Gallen to pay the levy unchanged until a legal clarification with the Stifft of Konstanz has taken place. Hans Wydehorn seals it.

Burgomaster and Council of Wangen inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that Kaspar Schwarz, who had been in dispute with the city of Lindau, has died and that his widow and her legal representatives, Heinrich Mülegg and Ital Syman, are now waiting for the pronouncement of the judgment, which St. Gallen has not yet pronounced after the previous hearing. The Wangen authorities request the written pronouncement of the judgment to the widow of Kaspar Schwarz.

Albrecht Kut asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for a written promise of safe conduct for himself and his companions, so that they could negotiate their dispute with Schwarz Hans Engler, which they regret, on the spot. Hans Murand seals it.

Burgomaster and Council of Überlingen inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen about a dispute between them and Count Johann von Werdenberg concerning several rights. Count Johann has now agreed with them that the case of Friedrich von Wartenberg, abbot of the Benedictine monastery on the Reichenau, is to be handed over. The abbot has now set a negotiation for 17 August in Überlingen. The Überlingen authorities ask the St. Gallen authorities to provide them with a Council delegation for support, preferably Ulrich Särri or Konrad Hör.

Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that on 27 August they will hold a negotiation in Wil with Junker and Freiherr Petermann von Raron and Knight Marquard Brisacher in the matter concerning the family Wälli. They ask the St. Gallen authorities to send them a Council delegation to support the negotiation.

Ammann and Council of Arbon report to Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that they had taken the St. Gallen citizen Ulrich Gutmann into custody because he had committed mischief against their citizen Hans Struss, which harmed him in honor, life, and property. They had, however, released Gutmann at the request of his friends and against surety until 24 August. The Arboners also take the following position regarding the place of the court hearing. If Gutmann had been a St. Gallen citizen at the time of his arrest, St. Gallen would be the court venue. Since this is not the case, they consider it unjustified that Gutmann, as an Arbon citizen, should be brought before a St. Gallen court.

Burgomaster and Council of Überlingen inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that, because of their conflict with Count Johann von Werdenberg-Heiligenberg, they have another court hearing with the abbot of the Benedictine monastery on the Reichenau on 3 September in Überlingen. The Überlingen ask the St. Gallen to send them a Council delegation to Überlingen for support.

Burgomaster and Council of Wangen thank Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for the delivery of the legal decision regarding the citizen of Wangen, the widow of Kaspar Schwarz, and report that the woman is not in the city, which is why they cannot answer completely. As soon as she is back, however, they will question her about the letter from St. Gallen and then answer.

Ulrich and Albrecht Schenk von Landegg complain to the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that the citizen of St. Gallen, Peter Lautenschlager, does not abide by the judgment rendered in the dispute between Lautenschlager and their Högger vom Buech over livestock transit rights. They ask the St. Gallen authorities to admonish their citizen so that the Högger may continue to drive his livestock through there. Albrecht Schenk von Landegg seals it.
Verena Wieland, Hans Brunners Ehefrau, asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to inform her in writing by messenger why her husband has been placed in custody.

Burgomaster and Council of Lindau inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that, at the request of St. Gallen, they agree to a negotiation with the widow of Kaspar Schwarz, although she cannot claim any right to it. The Lindauers ask the St. Galleners to pass a judgment as soon as possible and to inform them of it.

Burgomaster and Council of Schaffhausen report to Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that they are being attacked by Hans von Rechberg and other nobles, who have gathered an army of soldiers on foot and on horse around them, and that villages in the surroundings have been burned and people stabbed. The attackers apparently want to separate the city of Schaffhausen from the Empire. They ask immediately for support with soldiers, guns and crossbowmen, as much as St. Gallen can provide.

Burgomaster and Council of Schaffhausen inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that the army commanded by Hans von Rechberg has withdrawn from Schaffhausen and marched towards Rottweil. They thank them for the support provided from St. Gallen.

Ammann and Council of Arbon write to the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen, saying that their Ammann and the Burgomaster of St. Gallen had indeed agreed not to pursue the conflict between a woman named Hug and other women of St. Gallen on the one hand and Leonhard Winzürn of Arbon on the other hand any further. However, Winzürn had already previously invoked the ecclesiastical court. The people of Arbon therefore ask the people of St. Gallen to ensure that their party complies with the rights due to Leonhard Winzürn.

Burgomaster and Council of Zürich report to Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that a dispute has broken out between the alliance of the Swabian Imperial Cities on the one hand and the cities of Schaffhausen and Rottweil on the other. The citizens of Zürich have tried in vain to mediate between the parties. Zürich has now asked Ulm to issue a summons for negotiations to Ulm. The citizens of Zürich ask the citizens of St. Gallen to also send a Council delegation to Ulm for negotiations on 14 January.

Ammann and Council of Schwyz report to Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen how, after the last meeting of the Confederates in Luzern, all parties had agreed to the farewell except Unterwalden. Schwyz now inquires in St. Gallen whether they wish to stand by their opinion and cooperate to move Unterwalden to accept the farewell. They ask for a written answer with the messenger.

Hans Fechter, Stadtknecht of Ulm, complains to the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that they had destroyed his garden and thrown earth against his house during the construction of the new wall and the new ditch around the Vorstadt. Other residents, to whom the same had happened, had been compensated, but he had not. He requests a hearing in St. Gallen and safe conduct on the way there and back. He also requests a written answer.

Freiherr Wolfahrt V. von Brandis informs the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that Burkhard, his bailiff at Vaduz, the bearer of this letter, is to speak with them about monetary matters, and asks them to treat him as if he himself were present.

Hans von Höchst reports to the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that he had been in the town on 14 April and had spoken with former Burgomaster Heinrich Zwick, who had promised him that he would bring his affairs before the Council of St. Gallen. He would, however, do this only if Lindau also asked him to do so. Since this had not yet happened despite their earlier promise, his affair was still pending. He asks the Burgomaster and Council to set a date for negotiations. Hans von Höchst encloses with the letter a no longer extant copy of a letter that he had sent to the parish priest of Lindau.

Burgomaster and Council of Kempten inform Burgomaster and Council of Lindau about a meeting between Duke Sigismund, Count Hugo von Montfort, Marquard von Schellenberg, Marquard von Ems, a Landenberger and several others, who would have overheard a St. Gallen man named Ulrich Ritz in an inn. They would have discussed that they wanted to jointly take an unnamed place by ship. It is not known when this was to happen, but Kempten wants to warn Lindau.

Adelheid Täuber, wife of Konrad Lienhard, asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to let her back into the city (St. Gallen), after she was able to reach an agreement with her husband before an ecclesiastical court. She asks for a written answer to an address in Konstanz.
The envoys of the Confederate cities assembled in Zürich ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to remit a penalty for their (St. Gallen) town guard Jakob am Bühl.

Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz report to Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that unnamed servants of Konstanz had committed a crime near the house of Schnell, whereby one of them, who was not their citizen, had perished and the others were now on the run. Konstanz assures St. Gallen that they (Konstanz) would treat the citizen of St. Gallen, who was involved in the matter, no differently than all others.
Burgomaster and Council of Lindau inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that they would have informed Hans von Höchst to set the presentation of evidence in his case for 14 October.

Burgomaster and Council of Pfullendorf and of Radolfzell inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that they are to hold a negotiation together with the abbot of Reichenau in Konstanz, in which a homicide on Reichenau is to be discussed, and ask St. Gallen to send a delegation of the Council to support them.

The Council delegation of the allied Imperial cities in Schwaben asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for help in the deaths of Schürgi and Brechthans. They ask St. Gallen to contact their citizen Burkhard Schenk, a friend of the deceased Brechthans. He is to speak with the acquaintances of the deceased so that they do not take revenge on the cities, in particular Pfullendorf and Radolfzell. The cities ask for a written answer with the messenger.

Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for their assistance in the dispute between Konrad von Fulach and Konrad Ehinger, citizen of Konstanz, which was heard before the Bishop of Konstanz, with the support of Johannes Widenbach and the Säckelmeister of Zürich. However, no judgment was rendered at this first hearing; this is to take place at a further hearing. Konstanz asks St. Gallen whether its Burgomaster could be present at a renewed hearing on 9 December. They ask for a written answer with the messenger.

Burgomaster and Council of Esslingen inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that they are aware that the people of St. Gallen have taken several young rioters prisoner, some of whom have fled. The people of Esslingen have taken two men prisoner who were presumably involved and from whom they would have received a few names. Esslingen asks St. Gallen to communicate whether these names are known to anyone in St. Gallen and whether they could be associated with the rioters. If so, this person should be sent to Esslingen to identify the two detainees.

Burgomaster and Council of Lindau report to Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen in the negotiation matter concerning Hans von Höchst, how he (Hans von Höchst) did not observe the announced negotiation date contrary to his promises. Now they ask St. Gallen to continue to support them in the matter and ask for a written answer with the messenger.

Burkhard Schenk von Kastell writes to Ulrich Särri, Burgomaster of St. Gallen, that Hans Heger has informed him that a woman is leading his son into great expenses. Should this woman turn to Ulrich Särri, Burkhard Schenk asks that she be referred to his court in Roggwil, where both parties reside.

Burgomaster and Council of Rottweil report to Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that they had been very satisfied with the mediation of St. Gallen in a dispute between the alliance of the Swabian Imperial Cities on the one hand and the city of Schaffhausen and themselves on the other hand, which is why they again ask St. Gallen for mediation in a further negotiation on 4 May in Konstanz between the same parties.

Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz report to Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that in the dispute between Konrad von Fulach and the citizen of Konstanz Konrad Ehinger the Elder, in which a negotiation had already taken place through the mediation of the Bishop of Konstanz, the former Burgomaster of St. Gallen Johannes Widenbach as well as the Säckelmeister of Zürich Brennwart, no judgment had yet been pronounced. The citizen of Konstanz Ehinger had already requested the Bishop multiple times to render the judgment; the latter, however, wished to do so only if all mediators were present. St. Gallen should therefore send the aforementioned to Konstanz, and they ask for a written reply with the same messenger.

Burgomaster and Council of Überlingen ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to send a delegation of the Council to a negotiation in Sigmaringen on 29 July in their support, at which the matter concerning Konrad Schürpf von Freudenberg and his helpers is to be discussed. He has declared war on Überlingen, whereupon the city has summoned Count Johann von Werdenberg as mediator. Überlingen asks for a written answer with the messenger.

Burgomaster and Council of Wangen inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen about a certain Antonius Müller, who, although he wishes to abide by the Emperor's peace decree, has declared war on the city of Wangen and will not allow himself to be corrected by Wangen. He had been employed by the city of Wangen and had been fully paid. Wangen now asks St. Gallen to support them and to arrange a negotiation. Should Müller refuse a negotiation, Wangen asks to be informed about it. Wangen asks for a written reply with the same messenger.

Ammann and Council of Arbon reply to Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen in the matter between Hans Harscher and Konrad Bäldi, both citizens of St. Gallen, and Hans Strauss, citizen of Arbon, that Arbon and Marquard von Ems had tried in vain to convince Strauss to drop the matter. However, Strauss has agreed to participate in a hearing in Arbon within the next 14 days. Arbon asks the St. Gallen authorities for a written answer as to whether they and their party are in agreement with this.

Brun von Tettikofen, called Bindrich von Konstanz, bailiff at Altnau, informs the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that several people from Altnau would attempt to obtain the citizenship of St. Gallen, but must not be granted it, as they had previously been countrymen of Appenzell and their country right had now been revoked by the Confederates. He requests St. Gallen to reject any possible application for admission to citizenship, and reminds them that this would be under penalty of the Empire.

Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that they had been asked by some people to release the poor journeyman Burkhard Bruder, who had attacked the son of the St. Gallen citizen Heinrich Appenzeller in Konstanz and had therefore been sentenced to two years' imprisonment in the Turm. Konstanz had acceded to this wish. They now ask St. Gallen to question Appenzeller's son whether he agrees with this. Konstanz is willing to keep Bruder in prison at Appenzeller's expense. Konstanz wishes for a written answer from St. Gallen with the same messenger.

Burgomaster and Council of Ulm report to Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that their citizen Franz Schlicher had lent 50 gulden to Otmar Herr, which the St. Gallen Councilor Rudolf Friedbolt had given to Otmar Herr. Herr had sold Wachs in Ulm and should have settled his debts with the proceeds, but he had not done so. Since there are still more debtors of Franz Schlicher in St. Gallen, St. Gallen is to assist Hans Mayer, the authorized servant of Franz Schlicher, in collecting the debts in St. Gallen.

Johann von Hinwil, Abbot of the Benedictine monastery on the Reichenau, reports to the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that he has learned with dismay that the citizen of St. Gallen Konrad Lienhard has been attacked. The questioning of his officials has not led to the identification of the robber with the St. James' sign, although he has already been seen. He has forgotten a good binding knife in the inn and will probably return; his officials have in any case been alerted.

Burgomaster and Council of Überlingen report to Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that they have received the letter from St. Gallen concerning Hans Golder and that they will ensure that such shameful conduct is curbed. However, the citizens of Überlingen do not yet know how the citizens of Ravensburg, who had handed over Golder and Jöriglin to their prison, will proceed against them. Therefore, they cannot yet provide any further information.

Burgomaster and Council of Rottweil ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to hear their fellow citizen Heinz Burnberg, who brings the present letter to them, and to support him in the conflict with a St. Gallen piper.

Burgomaster and Council of Lindau again request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to send them a Council delegation on 19 June to support a negotiation, as the last negotiation with Count Ulrich did not take place.

Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen, with a copy enclosed in this letter, that they have heard of disturbances in Thurgau. Part of the disturbers comes from Uttwil and Kesswil, the other part consists of citizens of St. Gallen. Konstanz now asks St. Gallen to calm its citizens and asks for a written answer with the same messenger.

Ulrich Spät von Rorschach informs the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that, as decided in a past court hearing, he has acted in the dispute with Hans Zerahoch over a tithe as was decided. However, he (Spät) owes Zerahoch no tithe. Since the case has now been referred to the Pfalzgericht of the Benedictine Abbey of St. Gallen, he will do what is decided there.

Burgomaster and Council of Zürich inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that last night a break-in occurred in their Kaufhaus and cloths were stolen. They ask St. Gallen to hold back the cloths as well as the persons associated with them, should the goods be offered for sale in St. Gallen.

Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen about their efforts to settle the dispute between the St. Gallen citizen and councilor Kaspar Wirth and the Konstanz citizen Hans Muntprat (von Spiegelberg) the Younger. According to the accounts of Hans Muntprat, Kaspar Wirth claims to have bought the same vineyard in Berneck in the Rhine Valley from Marquard von Ems as he himself did. Konstanz asks St. Gallen for understanding that they could not take any action against their citizen, as the court proceedings in Berneck had not yet led to a result.

Burgomaster and Council of Memmingen thank Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for their mediation in the conflict with Count Wilhelm von Sargans, who has taken several citizens of Memmingen and of Wangen prisoner. The conflict is unfortunately not yet ended; on 11 November there is to be a negotiation as to whether the prisoners are to remain in prison. Memmingen asks St. Gallen to send a Council delegation to Feldkirch on 9 November. They have sent the same request to Lindau.

Schultheiss and Council of Bern report to Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that Grete, the wife of the St. Gallen citizen Ulrich, Master Bell-founder, has separated from her husband, as he has involved himself with another woman. Now he has asked his wife to return to him, which she gladly does on the condition that the other woman be expelled. Bern now asks, on behalf of Grete, that the said woman be expelled from the city.

Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz report to Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that on the past 9. September a servant of Burkhard Schenk von Kastell wanted to be admitted into their city, but this was not permitted to him because of his improper behavior. He had not wanted to hand over his knife to the gatekeepers and had threatened that he would come back with fire. Konstanz had subsequently summoned Burkhard Schenk multiple times to a court hearing, but he had never reacted to this. The people of Konstanz ask the people of St. Gallen to speak with Burkhard Schenk and to support them in this matter. In addition, they ask for a written answer with the same messenger.

Burgomaster and Council of Lindau inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that they wish to assemble in Lindau on 10 January in matters of fishing. Since the ordinance to date binds the area between the Schussenkopfs and Rheinhorn, but not yet the area below, Lindau asks St. Gallen to send a Council delegation to this negotiation date.

Burgomaster and Council of Lindau ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to support them with a Council delegation at a court hearing that they must hold with Count Ulrich von Montfort. This is to take place on 14 March in Wolfartsweiler. They ask the St. Gallen Council delegation to arrive in Lindau on the evening before.

Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that merchants on Lake Constance are no longer safe and that goods are being stolen from them, as recently happened to Nurembergers. Since this is harmful to all cities around Lake Constance, Konstanz invites the cities of its league to a consultation on 14. March in Konstanz. Although St. Gallen is not a member of the league, the Konstanzer ask the St. Gallen to send a Council delegation

Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz write to Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that they had invited Council delegations from St. Gallen and Appenzell to Konstanz on 9 May to deliberate on security in the land. Since St. Gallen has not been able to send a Council delegation, Appenzell and Konstanz have conducted the talks without St. Gallen. Konstanz promises to provide a written version of the talk for the purpose of a statement. Furthermore, the Konstanzer inform, with an enclosure, that they had issued a declaration with their neighbors.

Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz write to Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen regarding their talks with the Appenzellers to secure peace in the land. The Konstanzer have, as promised, informed the St. Galler, who could not be present at the talks, in writing about the results. The Konstanzer wanted to know within eight to ten days how St. Gallen stood on this. The Konstanzer now ask the St. Galler to communicate their position to Konstanz with the same messenger. In the case of approval, the Konstanzer also ask the St. Galler to inform the Appenzellers and to ensure the enforcement of the measures taken.

Rudolf Friedbolt, citizen of St. Gallen, informs the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that he has meanwhile obtained a position in Ravensburg, but that the plague has broken out there. He wishes to return to St. Gallen, but has obligated himself not to leave Ravensburg without the consent of St. Gallen. He now earnestly asks St. Gallen to allow him to leave Ravensburg with honor and to provide him with temporary work in St. Gallen.

Burgomaster and Council of Ravensburg inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that they have a court hearing on 18 July in Radolfzell with Hans Ulrich von Stoffeln, Hans von Rechberg von Hohenrechberg, their Lord of St. Georg and the family of Herbertshofen. They ask St. Gallen to send a Council delegation to support them there.

Burgomaster and Council of Wangen inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that they have to appear on 20 July in a matter concerning their hospital at a court hearing in St. Gallen at the Hofgericht in the palace of the Benedictine monastery. The Wangen hospital administrator, the bearer of this letter, is equipped with power of attorney for the proceedings. Wangen asks St. Gallen for support for their hospital administrator at the said hearing with two St. Gallen Council delegations.

Burgomaster and Council of Lindau write, at the request of Hans Arger of Lindau, the bearer of this letter, to Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen. Arger has heard that St. Gallen is seeking a new schoolmaster. The Lindauers recommend him for the appointment as schoolmaster in St. Gallen.

Jos Gössler, who had previously collected the old taxes in St. Gallen for three years, writes to Heinrich Zwick, Burgomaster of St. Gallen, that he has not yet received his promised wage of three pounds from the then Säckelmeister Senn. He asks that the money be sent to him through his brother-in-law Peter Herren, the bearer of the letter, as he needs the money in Lindau. He sends greetings to Zwick's wife and his son Michael.

Jos Gössler asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for the umpteenth time to send him his outstanding wages of three pounds. The Council had awarded him this sum, and the Säckelmeister Senn at the time had been ordered to pay him, which had not happened. He asks that the money be handed over to his brother-in-law, the bearer of the letter.

Ammann and Council of Altstätten inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that recently a servant named Hans Dürr died and left behind six small children. Since the widow is so poor and the children are still so small that they could not support their mother, Altstätten asks St. Gallen to take two of the children into its hospital until they can support themselves.

Urban von Widenbach, son of the late St. Gallen Burgomaster Johannes von Widenbach, asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen (unclear addressee) for help in the matter concerning the castle Zwingenstein in the Rheintal, which was destroyed by the Appenzellers. Castle Zwingenstein had been granted to his father by Duke Sigismund von Habsburg-Österreich, as he had been loyal to him and to King Friedrich IV von Habsburg-Österreich. His father had already complained to the Confederates that the castle should be returned to him, but the Appenzellers had not agreed to this for a long time, and his father has since died. He now asks the St. Gallen, as heir, to advocate for him with the Confederates so that he may take up his paternal inheritance.

Rudolf Ramsperg, priest, reports to the Burgomaster, City Ammann, Councilors, and Guild Masters of St. Gallen that he has become the victim of slander. A priest at Ems, with the support of Marquard von Ems, had accused him of having stolen a chasuble there. In his current place of activity, Davos, the slander had continued, and he had been reported to the Bishop of Chur. Since he is not being given a legal hearing, he asks St. Gallen to request in writing that the citizens and the Bishop of Chur treat him justly.
Emperor Friedrich III. instructs the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to lift the punishment against Ulrich Rietmüller.
Konrad Albrecht, town clerk of Konstanz, asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to support him in the debt collection from the citizen of St. Gallen Konrad Utz.

Janot Fulschill, Ammann, and the community of Bivio write to the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen. The people of St. Gallen are the founders and users of their church, which is why especially their merchants have privileges in Bivio. Bivio has built a new altar, and they now ask for relics, altar cloths, and vestments.

Burgomaster and Council of Biberach describe to Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen a dispute between Jakob Schad the Younger, citizen of Biberach, and hunters of Count Eberhard zu Kirchberg the Elder, which ended in a melee. Count Eberhard the Younger had thereupon, together with Duke Otto von Bayern and others, declared enmity against Biberach. Previous mediation negotiations and proposals for a solution had led to no result. Biberach asks St. Gallen to defend them against defamations before or after the next negotiation, which is to take place on 29 November in Memmingen. Biberach asks for a written answer with the messenger.

Heinrich Trösch von Walsee complains to the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen about the St. Gallen Hans Opfertshofer, because the latter interferes in his financial affairs and thereby angers his creditors. He says that this is all the more aggravating for him, as he is in a legal proceeding. He asks St. Gallen to persuade Hans Opfertshofer to leave him in peace, otherwise he sees himself compelled to seek a court hearing in St. Gallen on this matter. He asks for a written answer with the same messenger.

Hans Zerahoch von Rorschach, citizen of St. Gallen, writes to the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen regarding the conflict with his stepsons Rudolf and Egli Bertschi. The knight Heinrich von Randegg has referred the case to St. Gallen. He now asks St. Gallen for a court hearing and safe conduct in the name of Ulrich Rösch, the churchwarden. Furthermore, he asks for a written answer to the house of Klaus Blarer in Konstanz.

Burgomaster and Council of Lindau ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to set a new date for a court hearing in the dispute between them and the Schwarz, after a date had already been set but then cancelled. Lindau asks for a written answer with the messenger.

Burgomaster and Council of Zürich inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that those mentioned in a sealed enclosure had declared war on them, the citizens of St. Gallen, and the two associated Confederates as helpers of Reinhard von Schauenburg.

Burkhard II. von Randegg, Bishop of Konstanz, asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to remit the remaining three pounds of a fine of six pounds in total, to which Hans Maurer von Obersteinach was sentenced by the city of St. Gallen. He asks for a reply.

Ulrich Rösch, Abbot of the Benedictine monastery of St. Gallen, informs the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that, because of the letters allegedly sent from the monastery's chancery to Stühlingen, another date for the court hearing has been set. This takes place on 11 June in Wil, and they meet on the evening before.

Ammann and Council of Arbon confirm to Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that they have received and understood their letter regarding their citizen Hans Mötteli. They are, however, of the opinion that the St. Gallen people have not understood the cause of the dispute between Arbon and Mötteli and the judgment pronounced by the Bishop of Konstanz, which is why the Arbon people propose a clarifying meeting with the Bishop.

Jakob Trapp, Hofmeister and bailiff of Bregenz, asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to send him the midwife from Kempten, who is staying in St. Gallen, so that she can take care of his heavily pregnant wife. He asks for a written answer with the messenger as to whether and for how long St. Gallen can do without the midwife.

Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen order Ammann and Judges of Balgach, citizens of St. Gallen, not to further pursue the women of Grünenstein regarding the open questions of judicial jurisdictions. St. Gallen will directly contact the Kanonissenstift in Lindau, in whose court Balgach and the von Grünenstein would be located, and afterwards inform Balgach.

Der Prokurator Georg Rem informs Johannes Utz, Stadtschreiber zu St. Gallen, about the dispute concerning von Reischach and writes what he has already done in this matter. Furthermore, he reports that Bilgeri von Heudorf will come to Konstanz and that he has no powers of attorney in a damages claim concerning Burkhard von Homburg.

Johannes Utz, town clerk, reports to the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen on his negotiations with the Lords of Österreich, which he had conducted there together with others on behalf of St. Gallen. They had learned that the person sought is a servant of Duke Ludwig IX. of Bayern-Landshut and resides in the castle at Gundelfingen. To save on expenses, they had decided that Herr Marquard, Leonhard Merz and Konrad should continue riding, while Johannes Utz himself, together with Othmar Hux, wishes to remain in Landshut to await the answer of Duke Ludwig IX. to their written petition.

Georg Rem reports to Johannes Utz, town clerk of St. Gallen, that Burkhard von Homburg is of the opinion that he can free himself from the ban. Rem also asks for information and instructions, particularly regarding the claim for damages.

Georg Rem informs the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen about the negotiations in the case of the ban into which Burkhard von Homburg has fallen. He writes that an extension of the deadline has been granted and that the next negotiation on this matter is to take place on 13 December. Then the town clerk (Johannes Utz) is to be present, and new letters of attorney for the clerk and his companion are to be issued. The matter concerning Bilgeri has also been adjourned. Finally, he reports that he has promised the messenger a payment of six Bohemian.

Georg Rem informs Johannes Utz, town clerk of St. Gallen, that in the case of the outlawry of Burkhard von Homburg, the Council of St. Gallen was once again granted an extension of the deadline. Rem advises renewing and adapting the letter of attorney, and he gives precise instructions to that effect. The matter concerning Bilgeri is still pending.

Georg von Rechberg zu Hohenrechberg and Bero von Rechberg zu Hohenrechberg, brothers, explain to the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen their view of the matter in the dispute with Michael von Friedberg. They say that they had requested the Emperor for a judgment, who had ordered them to deposit 3000 gulden principal in Ulm, which they had done. They ask St. Gallen not to take sides for Michael von Friedberg any further. Attached to the letter is a copy of an imperial summons to a hearing, which is dated on the 20. February 1465.

Georg von Rechberg zu Hohenrechberg and Bero von Rechberg zu Hohenrechberg, brothers, explain to the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen their view of the matter in the dispute with Michael von Friedberg. They say that they had requested the Emperor for a judgment, who had ordered them to deposit 3000 gulden principal in Ulm, which they had done. They ask St. Gallen not to take sides for Michael von Friedberg any further. Attached to the letter is a copy of an imperial summons to a hearing, dated 20 February 1465.

Walter Spättig asks Hans Schürpf, Burgomaster of St. Gallen, to act against rumors being spread about him in the hospital. He is accused by various people of having abused a lame girl in the hospital. To prove his innocence, he asks that the girl be questioned by the hospital master outside the hospital about who instigated her to tell such lies. If the girl should refuse to make a statement, she is to be examined by women outside the hospital. Spättig asks that his case be brought before the hospital outer masters and the Council and that he be given safe conduct until Easter. In addition, he asks for a written answer.

Hans Stuss requests, on behalf of his mentally ill maid Verena, the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to take her son Hans into their care. Contrary to the statement of Ulrich Gelter, Hans is already older than 14 years.

Schultheiss and Council of Frauenfeld inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that Hugo von Landenberg and Michael Zwick could not keep the date of the court hearing of 28 March, as Hugo von Landenberg would have to attend another court date on that day. They ask for a new date for the hearing.

Wolfhard VI. von Brandis answers the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that, upon their letter, he has instructed his Ammann on the Eschnerberg to mediate in the dispute between Hans Riner von Salez and Lienhard Signer vom Eschnerberg.

Wolfhard VI. von Brandis informs the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen in the dispute between his subordinate Lienhard Signer on the one hand and Hans Riner von Salez, the subordinate of Lütfried Mötteli, on the other hand, that he has taken up the matter of the dispute. He now asks the St. Gallen authorities, in the name of Signer, to ensure that Signer receives his due. Should this not happen, he says that he will not prevent Signer from pursuing the case further in court. He asks for a written answer.

Burgomaster and Council of Zürich report to Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that Othmar Ortwin has complained to them that he was not treated properly at the court hearing in the Pfalz in St. Gallen. Ortwin wishes that his case be re-heard in Wil with impartial vassals. If the St. Gallen authorities are not in agreement with this, the case is to be heard by a Confederate arbitral tribunal or another body agreeable to them. They ask for a written reply with the same messenger.

Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen write to Burgomaster and Council of Zürich regarding their citizen Otmar Ortwin. He has complained to them that he was not treated properly at the court hearing in the Pfalz in St. Gallen and that his escort protection was not upheld. Ortwin wishes for his case to be re-heard in Wil with impartial vassals. If the St. Gallen authorities do not agree to this, the case should be heard by a Confederate arbitral court or another body acceptable to them. After the case is recapitulated as described in the letter from Zürich, the reasons are listed for why the trial of Othmar Ortwin proceeded lawfully. St. Gallen insists on the Pfalz court of St. Gallen as the place of hearing and asks Zürich to ensure, in the event of Ortwin's resistance, that he accepts the judgment. The St. Gallen authorities ask for a reply with the messenger.

Burgomaster and Council of Zürich answer, on behalf of their citizen Otmar Ortwin, Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen in the case of his rejected inheritance claim. He objects to the composition of the Pfalzgericht as well as to the failure to observe the safe conduct. Despite his appeal and request for the resumption of the proceedings, he has not yet received an answer. Zürich asks for support so that the matter can be settled as soon as possible and without further expenses. The Zürich side asks for a written answer with the messenger.

The Confederate councils assembled in Rapperswil call on the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to end the inheritance dispute between them and the citizen of Zürich Othmar Ortwin. They offer themselves as an arbitral tribunal. A written reply is expected in Zürich within eight days.

Georg Rem writes to Johannes Utz, town clerk of St. Gallen, regarding the lawsuits with Burkhard von Homburg, the lords of Klingenberg, of Landenberg and of Friedingen. Rem complains that he is not sufficiently informed about the indictment at the court in Rottweil. He would have written to St. Gallen earlier, however the messenger Siferlin did not ride. In addition, the city of St. Gallen still owes him money; Rem asks for the settlement of the open accounts.

Georg Rem writes to Johannes Utz, town clerk in St. Gallen, and inquires about the outstanding three gulden, which he had already demanded in writing earlier. The messenger Siferlin had told him that in St. Gallen they thought the amount of three gulden had already been settled, which, however, is not the case.

Ammann and Council of Arbon confirm to Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen their inquiry, that the child (possibly Ursula Schüb) of the St. Gallen citizen Gnäpser and of the deceased father of the child Hans Schüb of Arbon, as well as children of other St. Gallen citizens, are under guardianship according to town law.
Hans Wilhelm von Friedingen zu Hohenkrähen writes to the Councils of the Confederates assembled in Konstanz concerning his debts.

The Confederate councils assembled in Baden ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for support in the matter of the hospital almsman Walter Spättig from Appenzell. Due to a slander, he was expelled from the hospital and from the city of St. Gallen. They now ask that he be reinstated in his living. A response is expected at the Diet in Zürich.

Georg Rem asks Johannes Utz, town clerk in St. Gallen, in a letter written in haste, for the settlement of the expenses which, in his opinion, have not yet been paid. For examination, he encloses a calculation sheet.
Georg Rem lists to Johannes Utz, town clerk in St. Gallen, his expenses and asks for examination and payment.
Georg Rem asks Johannes Utz, town clerk in St. Gallen, once again to settle his monetary claims. He says that he has not yet received any answer to his letters and asks for one.

Georg Rem writes to Johannes Utz, town clerk in St. Gallen, that he has received his audit. He agrees with it and now asks for rapid payment. He further asks for written consent that he give the letters to a messenger. He further asks that a leather sack be given to Hans Zerahoch.

Georg Rem complains to Johannes Utz, town clerk in St. Gallen, about the lack of trust towards him and that the commission as Prokurator has been withdrawn from him. There would still be much to do at the Hofgericht, and one could have found an agreement regarding the differences concerning wages, but now his joy has passed. Nevertheless, Rem assures that he would not accept a possible mandate of the opposing party.

Georg Rem urgently requests Johannes Utz, town clerk in St. Gallen, for information regarding the letters of outlawry and debt concerning the Lords of Klingenberg, Homburg and Friedingen. He lists the costs for new copies. He advises him to send the old documents, otherwise expenses for the search in the outlawry book will arise. Furthermore, he requests to be informed whether the documents are to be authenticated with more expensive attached seals or only with impressed seals.

The brothers Wolfhart and Sigmund von Brandis ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to instruct their town clerk to redeem the writ of judgment drawn up for their subjects of Triesen and the subjects of Sevelen belonging to their cousin Count Wilhelm von Montfort, in favor of the Triesen people, since they are poor people, for a modest fee.

Georg Rem writes in haste to Johannes Utz, town clerk of St. Gallen, regarding various legal matters. He sends four Achtbriefe, which cost ten schillings. Should an Achtbrief also be drawn up in the matter of Burkhard von Homburg and Hans Wilhelm von Friedingen, he would have to pay for the search in the Achtbuch at the chancery. Thereupon Rem advises against suing von Mering. He lists the various costs and the messenger's fee. He assures that he will do his utmost in the St. Gallen affairs, for he has done nothing else all day today but attend to their messenger. He sends back the old Achtbriefe and other documents and asks for instructions.

Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen write to the Bishop of Passau, who, according to his own account, has acted as Chancellor of the Emperor in pursuit of freedoms for St. Gallen. He demands in a letter 400 gulden as a fee. The people of St. Gallen reply that they had given no one a mandate, except that they had been in contact with Master Heinrich, who had been at the court in Konstanz last summer. It had been agreed that he would advocate for the acquisition of freedoms for St. Gallen, but that the people of St. Gallen should decide for themselves on the acceptance after the submission of a proposal. Since the outcome does not correspond to the expectations of the people of St. Gallen, they are not willing to pay the high fee of 400 gulden. However, the people of St. Gallen are willing to pay something in addition to the 120 gulden already borrowed, provided that a freedom charter sealed by the Emperor is delivered, which corresponds to the copy attached to this letter.

Burgomaster and Council of Kempten send to Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen a letter of recommendation for their citizen Benz Brun and his son. He wishes to purchase a hospital benefice in the Holy Spirit Hospital in St. Gallen for himself and his son.

Burgomaster and Council of Lindau invite Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to a meeting on Sunday 31. January in their city. There, the problem of overfishing of Lake Constance is to be discussed and solutions for the Common Benefit are to be found.

Burgomaster and Council of Zürich write to Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen regarding their citizen Jodokus Krum, abbot of the monastery of St. Georg in Stein am Rhein, who is in dispute with Hans von Adlikon from Bischofszell and Elisabeth Huwin, Konrad Wettler’s wife and a citizen of St. Gallen. Despite a judgment from the court of St. Gallen, which Hans von Adlikon now accepts, Elisabeth Huwin appeals before the imperial court. The Zürichers ask the St. Galleners to ensure that the appeal of their citizen is withdrawn and that she also accepts the judgment.

The Imperial Cities on Lake Constance Konstanz, Überlingen, Lindau, Ravensburg, Wangen and Isny ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for support in the dispute of Hans Sporer of Buchhorn against Anna Seger. Anna Seger has a supporter named Hans Sprotz of Luzern, who is allegedly staying on St. Gallen territory and who does not want to recognize the judgment. St. Gallen should not give Sprotz shelter and should ensure that he follows the ordinary legal process. They ask for a written answer with the messenger.

The town council of München addresses the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen in the matter of their citizen Jörg Kramer. They ask for the restitution of his trade goods stolen from him on the lake at Meersburg or of the corresponding equivalent of 30 gulden. Kramer has debts, but is diligent and must provide for his wife and child.

Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for support in a matter against their citizen Hans Witzig, who is called the Swiss. Hostility has been declared against him by several journeymen in Bregenz. Witzig has now sworn under oath that he knew nothing of it and is not aware of any guilt, which is why his safety should be guaranteed. The people of Konstanz ask for a written answer with the messenger.

Burgomaster and Council of Zürich ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for support in a conflict over a monetary claim of six gulden by the St. Gallen citizen Konrad Flar from Konstanz against the prioress and the convent of the monastery of Töss. Flar threatens to bring the monastery before a foreign court. This is to be prevented, and the case is to be handled either by the Burgomaster and Council of Zürich or the Schultheiss and Council of Winterthur. The Zürich side asks for a written answer with the messenger.

The Confederate council envoys assembled in Zürich write to the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen in the dispute between the citizen of Zürich Martin Benz and the Unterwaldner peasant Hans von Eggenberg on the one hand, and the citizens of St. Gallen Strauss and their partner Klaus Stoss on the other. They say that they had asked the St. Gallen authorities for treatment in the great Council, but that no answer had yet been given. They now ask for the release of the correspondence. Furthermore, the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen are to release the surety of the Strauss, since they are in any case citizens of Zürich and resident there. They ask for a written answer with the same messenger.

Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz call upon Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to send a Council delegation to Lindau on 16. August. Knight Marquard IV. von Ems takes up again an old dispute of his deceased father Marquard III. The people of Lindau now approach the Imperial cities of Überlingen, Ravensburg, Memmingen, Kempten, Wangen, Isny, Buchhorn and Leutkirch, who were allied with one another at that time, with a request for support. The further course of action is to be discussed at the assembly, in particular the question of whether Lindau itself or the cities jointly should respond. Copies are delivered for preparation.

Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen request Count Ulrich V. of Württemberg, in the name of their citizen Kunigunde von Altstätten, widow of Hans Thumb von Neuburg, to grant her and her children support in their affairs and not to give credence to slanders, this in view of the services rendered at that time by Hans Thumb and his brother Konrad in favor of the Count.

Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen presumably inform the Council of Winterthur that their citizen Simon Kunz has nothing to do with the dispute over outstanding interest with Schultheiss Erhart Hunzikon, and that Egli von Lörn, who must pay the interest, wishes to settle the disputes.

Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen inform Burgomaster and Council of Nürnberg, at their request, that they will reprimand the citizen of St. Gallen Erhart Geisser in his dispute with citizens of Nürnberg. They say that they have no competence to do so, because Geisser had already renounced his citizenship of St. Gallen on 26 September.

Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen inform Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz that the former Burgomaster of St. Gallen, Hans Schürpf, had been in Konstanz to complain about the buying and selling of calves that were too young, which violates the Konstanz butchers' regulation. The St. Gallen side takes note that the Konstanz butchers deny this upon inquiry by their authorities, and that the authorities then instructed the butchers once again to observe the regulation. The Konstanz side had in turn asked the St. Gallen authorities to also instruct their butchers to comply with the regulation. The St. Gallen side now informs the Konstanz side that they had done so.

Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen presumably inform the Council of Winterthur that they had spoken with their citizen Simon Kunz so that he would pay the outstanding interest, which still originated from Simon's father Hans Kunz, to Erhard Hunzikon, Schultheiss of Winterthur, holder of the bond. Kunz maintains that half of the debt had been repaid and therefore a lower interest would have been paid. The St. Gallen authorities ask that Hunzikon travel to St. Gallen to settle the matter

The Confederate council envoys at the Diet in Zürich inform the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that Othmar Ortwin has complained to them that the inheritance of his deceased brother has not yet been handed over to him, although they had written to the citizens of St. Gallen on this matter from Rapperswil on 6 September 1470. They therefore once again urge the citizens of St. Gallen to put Ortwin into his inheritance. They ask for a written answer with the messenger.

Jakob Gir von Steinach writes to the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen, saying that the citizen of St. Gallen Nänger has seized his property. Since Gir cannot attend to it at present, he asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to find out why Nänger did this. Furthermore, he asks that the matter be heard before them on 16 October. He asks for a reply.

Burgomaster and Council of Zürich inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that the eidgenössischen Bünde are to be renewed on 19 May, and call upon the citizens and envoys of St. Gallen to assemble on that day.

The Confederate envoys at the Diet in Schaffhausen write to the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that a delegation of the Abbot of Salem had appeared before them and informed them that several of his dependents of the abbey had appealed to the Emperor against a judgment of the Bishop of Konstanz in a dispute between the dependents of the abbey and the predecessor of the Abbot, although they had promised not to do so. Furthermore, the Abbot had learned that the dependents of the abbey had, among other things, sought support from the people of St. Gallen. The envoys of the Diet ask the people of St. Gallen not to take up the cause of the dependents of the abbey. They ask for a written answer with the messenger.

Bishop Hermann Breitenlandenberg of Konstanz informs the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that he will not participate in a day set by the Abbot of the Benedictine Monastery of St. Gallen for 29 February regarding the dispute between the Bishop and the Abbot following the previous unsuccessful meeting in Wil, and that he has informed the Abbot of this by the accompanying letter. He thanks the citizens of St. Gallen for their support in settling the dispute.

Bishop Hermann of Konstanz urges the Abbot of St. Gallen, Ulrich Rösch, to settle the dispute, which has broken out because of the encroachments of St. Gallen churchmen on people of Bischofszell, before the Confederates, after the previous meeting at the castle in Wil has failed, as the Abbot has not pursued the guilty parties. The Bishop asks for a written answer with the messenger.

Bishop Hermann of Konstanz asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to settle the dispute between him and the Abbot of the Benedictine monastery of St. Gallen on the day appointed for 6 April in St. Gallen before the Komtur of Tobel, together with the knight Ludwig von Helmsdorf, Rudolf Giel von Glattburg and Dietrich in der Halden, former Ammann of Schwyz.

Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen inform Burgomaster and Council of Nördlingen that they wish to take the learned Ambrosius von Eberstein, who is engaged in medicine, into their service, and ask them to accommodate him regarding the Nachsteuer and the Abzug.

Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen ask Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz, in the name of the St. Gallen resident (Hintersasse) Heinrich Grüninger, called Eggshus, to grant him a safe conduct to Konstanz so that he can settle his dispute with the citizen of Konstanz Heinrich Schüchzer. Furthermore, Heinrich Grüninger is ready to submit to the court of Konstanz if Schüchzer's claims should be justified. The St. Gallen ask for an answer with the messenger.

Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen ask Jakob, who recently spoke with the wife of the St. Gallen citizen Heinrich Brunner, to capture him and hand him over to the St. Gallen, as he has not complied with the demands of the St. Gallen.

Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen ask Johann II. von Werdenberg, Bishop of Augsburg, to instruct his church administrator of Rettenberg, Hermann von Gottsfeld, to return the confiscated property of the St. Gallen citizen Heinz Mayer von Egg, as the Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz had determined in a legal ruling, after the Abbot of Kempten had decided that this dispute should be adjudicated there. The St. Gallen ask for a written reply with the messenger.

Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen ask the recipient, a Prince, to ensure that the St. Gallen citizen Heinrich Lehmann, called Vogelwaider, from whom 17 horses along with two new saddles, a crossbow, a bag, a gold ring, as well as gold and silver were taken in the land by Count Bernhard von Schomburg as he was travelling home from Österreich, has these things returned, as the recipient has promised the Confederate council envoys. The St. Gallen ask for a written answer with the messenger.

Dekan and Chapter of the Foundation at Konstanz answer the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that they reject the St. Gallen proposal that the people of Almensberg should hold court there until the dispute with Knight Ludwig von Helmsdorf and the bailiff of Arbon is settled, and suggest that the people of Almensberg let all court matters rest in the meantime. Should the St. Gallen not be in agreement, Dekan and Chapter offer to ask Ludwig von Helmsdorf whether he is in agreement with the St. Gallen proposal. They ask for a reply.

Dekan and Chapter of the Foundation at Konstanz ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to lend them four or five harquebuses for a short time, as the castle of Arbon is in danger. They ask for a written answer.

Otto IV. von Sonnenberg, Bishop-elect of Konstanz, sends the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen a German copy of his appeal against the appointment of Ludwig von Freiberg as Bishop of Konstanz by the Pope and urges the St. Gallen to announce this to the clergy and to support him, as required by the Emperor. He asks for a written reply with the messenger.

Ludwig von Freiberg, Bishop of Konstanz provided by the Pope and all the cardinals, urges the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to finally acknowledge the lawfulness of his claims to the bishopric within six days of receiving this letter, as Count Eberhard von Württemberg and the Austrian Duchess did. Should the citizens of St. Gallen let the deadline pass, he is compelled to impose the Church ban on them. He asks for a written answer.

The Statthalter of the Domdean and Chapter of the Stift of Konstanz inform the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that the opponent of the Cathedral Chapter in the dispute over the bishop's seat, Ludwig von Freiberg, has turned several of his allies against the Cathedral Chapter. The Cathedral Chapter asked Ludwig's allies to postpone all disputes until the diocesan dispute was settled, but Hans Thüring von Friedingen does not comply with this due to an old claim of his father Hans Wilhelm von Friedingen against Bishop Hermann von Breitenlandenberg. Although the Cathedral Chapter offered him legal redress and he has no document that would allow him to seize the debtor, he abducted people who were working in the episcopal town of Neunkirch in the Klettgau on 3 April to the castle of Hohenkrähen. In front of the Burgomaster and Council of Schaffhausen, of whom the Cathedral Chapter learned of this attack the following day, Hans Thüring justified this with outstanding debts of a Neukircher to one of his servants. The knightly society in the Hegau, which had been asked for help by the Cathedral Chapter, was also unable to move Hans Thüring to release the prisoners. Until 21 April he was not willing to settle the matter amicably, but declared the feud to the Cathedral Chapter together with his allies, who are named in an attached note. The attitude of Ludwig von Freiberg is unclear. The Statthalter and Chapter of Konstanz ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for help, especially in the protection of the priests.

Ludwig von Freiberg, provided Bishop of Konstanz, repeatedly urges the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen, in his reply to a letter from St. Gallen, to recognize him as Bishop within eight days, otherwise he will place them under the ban of the Church.

Notary Ulrich Berger, at the request and in the presence of the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen, draws up an instrument addressed to Pope Sixtus IV., in which the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen declare that they cannot comply with the papal request to recognize Ludwig von Freiberg as Bishop of Konstanz, citing their obligations to the Emperor and the decree of Pope Alexander III. that no disturbances should arise because of his commands, and they affirm that they are faithfully devoted to the Pope. They ask the Pope for an instrument. Present as witnesses are Lienhard Schickli von Speicher, a man of Appenzell, and Jörg Franz von München.

Schultheiss and Council of Luzern demand, in the name of the Confederation, that Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen immediately march out with their troops to support Bern against Duke Karl der Kühne of Burgund, who is besieging Murten.

Burgomaster and Council of Neuenburg am Rhein in the Breisgau request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to support the bearer of this letter in the collection of the debts of Elisabeth Kronauer, a resident of St. Gallen, against her citizen Konrad von Heitersheim, whose proxy is the messenger.

Ammann and Council of Uri thank Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for their support against the rule of Mailand and report how the troops remaining in the Leventina encountered over ten thousand enemies at Giornico on 28 December, killed a thousand of them and captured numerous weapons, although they themselves were only 600.

Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen ask the King of Frankreich to take in the Count of Limburg, who had been driven out by the Duke of Burgund several years ago, as a servant. He became a citizen of St. Gallen with his wife and children after his flight, among others to the Princes of Bayern, and has proven himself a reliable citizen.

Ammann and Council of Uri request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to hand over to Hans Wachs, the messenger of this letter, the money that the Urians have deposited with them on account of the Thurgau, and to support him in other ways as well, so that he can buy a little grain, which is scarce due to the prevailing high prices.

Ammann and Council of Schwyz request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to set a court day in the dispute between Knight Johann von Toggenburg, a subject of Schwyz, and his wife Maria von Ratzenhausen on the one hand, and those of Kempten and Neukirch on the other, after the St. Gallen had been appointed by the Confederates to settle this dispute, and those of Kempten and Neukirch had also requested a court day. The Schwyzers request a written reply with the same messenger.

Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to grant Mattheus Sailer, citizen of Konstanz and bearer of this letter, the rights of citizenship and guild membership, after he has settled in St. Gallen and married there, upon which the Konstanzer Sailer are released from their citizenship.

Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to settle the dispute between the abbot of the Benedictine monastery of St. Gallen and the Mistress and the nuns of Münsterlingen, who are under the citizenship of the citizens of Konstanz, although the citizens of St. Gallen have previously refused to do so. The citizens of Konstanz ask for an answer with the messenger.

Schultheiss and Council of Winterthur ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to support their citizen Johannes Fäs in obtaining from the St. Gallen citizen Heinrich Benn an extension of the deadline for the repayment of his debts, as Fäs cannot meet the originally agreed date because his debtors have not yet paid him.

Burgomaster and Council of Zürich ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to intervene with the von Wangen, who hold the citizenship of St. Gallen and who are mediating a dispute between the von Gams, who belong to Andreas Roll von Bonstetten, knight and citizen of Zürich, and the von Haag, so that the von Gams may retain what is theirs.

Schultheiss and Council of Luzern ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to contact Kaplan Rudolf Friedbolt, as his son of the same name, Rudolf, is in the Luzern hospital and suffers from madness, which the hospital master can no longer manage. Friedbolt should take his son to himself or financially relieve the hospital.

Burgomaster and Council of Ravensburg thank Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for their support in obtaining two relics of Saint Gallus and report that they received the relics, as befits, in a procession and transferred them to the parish church.

Schultheiss and Council of Luzern request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to admit Gärtler of Sursee, the husband of Adelheid Gärtler, to the inheritance of the deceased citizen of St. Gallen Elisabeth Locher, as his wife Adelheid is Elisabeth's nearest relative.

Burgomaster and Council of Isny inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that, at the request of the St. Gallen, they have spoken with the merchants of Isny and that these will use the St. Gallen inspection mark only for St. Gallen twill.

Burgomaster and Council of Überlingen inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that they set a court day in the dispute between Ulrich von Helmsdorf on the one hand and Konrad von Hersberg, citizen of Überlingen, on the other hand, which, however, did not take place. At the request of Jos Rudolf von Hersberg, father of Konrad, the Überlingen authorities proposed to Ulrich von Helmsdorf a court day before Count Georg and Ulrich von Werdenberg or the Austrian steward of the Landvogtei Schwaben, Marquard von Schellenberg, or before Burgomaster and Council of Ravensburg or Pfullendorf. Ulrich von Helmsdorf did not answer this proposal but told the Überlingen messenger orally that he would personally contact Rudolf. Burgomaster and Council of Überlingen therefore ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen not to support Ulrich von Helmsdorf should a dispute arise. They ask for a written answer with the same messenger.

Ammann and Council of Appenzell request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to assist the Appenzell countryman Konrad Huter, bearer of this letter, who has acquired a pledge, namely a house, from the deceased St. Gallen citizen and carrier Brenner, which was subsequently transferred to Huter, in his right, since the pledge had been sold unlawfully.

Ammann and Council of Uri inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that the citizen of St. Gallen Georg Wetter was killed by the Uri resident Bartholomäus Schüeli in Frankreich, where they met, after Schüeli had warned Wetter to stay away from him. Schüeli avenged the killing of his relative Merch Kirster of Unterwalden by Wetter, regarding which the people of Unterwalden wanted to inform the people of St. Gallen, but misplaced the letter. The friends of Wetter now want to avenge themselves on Schüeli again. The people of Uri now ask the people of St. Gallen to restrain the friends of Wetter from doing this, so that no greater harm occurs. They ask for a written answer.

Burgomaster and Council of Zürich inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that they have negotiated with the St. Gallen master builder during his visit to Zürich that he is to build a helmet on the Wasserkirche starting from 4 March 1487 and remain in Zürich during this time. They ask for the St. Gallen consent and that during this time the services of the master builder not be promised to anyone else.

Konrad Hür, executioner in Ulm and formerly in the service of Sigismund von Habsburg, Archduke of Österreich, offers his services as executioner to the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen, as he can no longer remain in Ulm from Whitsun of the following year, 3 June 1487, and the executioner of St. Gallen is ready to exchange with him. He asks for a written answer.

Ammann and Council of Feldkirch inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that their citizen Hans Kyber was ordered, due to a conflict settled by the Landschreiber of Appenzell, to pay the citizen of St. Gallen Rudolf Herr three pounds and five shillings on 13 January, to which he had consented. However, this did not happen, which is why Rudolf Herr is now proceeding to collect the money. Ammann and Council of Feldkirch therefore ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to make Rudolf Herr wait a little longer, as the deadline has only recently passed.

Schultheiss and Council of Solothurn inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that they did not reach an agreement with the servants who present this letter regarding an extension of their period of service, although they were willing to comply with their request for a higher wage, and the servants did not go to the Rhine to the fatally ill father of the trumpeter as announced, but to St. Gallen. The Solothurners are, however, nevertheless willing to comply with the St. Gallen request for the discharge of the servants.

Archduke Sigismund von Österreich asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to send him guns, powder, and saltpeter for his war against Venedig, for which he will show himself grateful to the city or pay for it. He asks for an answer.
